Head: `45b86a521b7d9336cab8c4297591aaf2fe9a4ccc`
Base (refreshed origin/main merge-base): `0ff8887e5e965400b01645ef40b85fd0b2605cf2`
Reviewer: `agent:codex-review-299`

## Blocking

1. **P1 — Normalize before startup conversation recovery, not only before workspace installation.** Changed call site: `Sources/Workspace.swift:267`. Unchanged consumers: `Sources/AppDelegate.swift:3416`, `:3457`, `:3469`; `Sources/Conversation/ScrapeCapturePipeline.swift:38`, `:263`; `Sources/Conversation/SnapshotBridge.swift:53`–`:66`.

   Concrete AC1/B024 input: take the synthetic duplicate-record fixture and give both A records `metadata.terminal_type = "codex"`. With the default conversation store enabled and scraper collection succeeding (an empty candidate batch is sufficient), startup loads the raw snapshot and builds two contexts for A before `Workspace.restoreSessionSnapshot` runs. `reconcileCodex` then passes both contexts to `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` at line 263. It traps on A, killing the process before the new normalization can repair the workspace. This is the ticket's duplicate-tab crash through the real startup path, not a speculative crash window.

   The same placement also violates the first-complete-record requirement without that crash: with terminal_type absent and conflicting active conversation refs on the two A records, the startup bridge writes the later ref over the first in `seedMap`. No scrape contexts are needed. The normalized workspace subsequently reads that store in `pendingRestartPlans` (`Workspace.swift:496`–`:500`), and normal snapshot capture writes its value back (`:916`). A discarded record can therefore supply the surviving tab's resumed/persisted conversation. The new tests omit conversation refs and call workspace restore directly, bypassing both startup consumers.

   Smallest fix: apply the existing workspace-local keep-first normalization to the loaded app snapshot before deriving activity floors, scrape contexts, or conversation seeds; use the resulting snapshot consistently for startup and workspace restore. Preserve drop diagnostics when moving the boundary. Keep a safe normalization boundary for direct/debug workspace restore callers. No new migration or identity mechanism is needed. Add behavioral regressions through startup snapshot preparation and bridge/reconciliation for duplicate Codex records and conflicting conversation refs, including a first record with no conversation and a later duplicate with one. Assert one retained context, no trap, and only the first record's conversation state (or absence) surviving seed/resume/save.

## Non-blocking

None.

The helper itself preserves the complete first record, first layout placement, surviving order, area sidecars, geometry, and existing unknown/empty-leaf fallback inputs. Workspace-local sets avoid conflating distinct UUIDs. Installation metadata and both workspace resume loops use its result. The changed production work is restore-only; no typing/socket hot-path changes, tenant-config writes, schema bump, submodule changes, or new localized product strings were found. Live pane dictionaries remain correctly untouched.

## Evidence and limits

One static pass covered all eight changed files and the startup, conversation, layout, metadata, selection, and save seams. No local builds, tests, or app launches were performed. The finding above is established by source control flow; it was not executed in this review.

Independently inspected exact-head CI run [36964399715](https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/actions/runs/36964399715/job/110704874838): app build passed; logic ran 2,041 tests, three skipped, zero failures. All six normalization cases, the new persistence case, and all five host TabIdentityRestoreTests individually passed. Host suite overall failed with 49 assertions across 44 cases; comparing its failed-case identities with [exact-base run 36943263290](https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/actions/runs/36943263290/job/110639439481) found identical sets. These passing targeted tests do not cover the blocking startup path. At inspection, GhosttyKit was queued and macOS Compatibility was in progress; no all-checks-green or landing verdict is claimed. Remote branch head and merge-base were rechecked before posting.

## Runtime proof still required

Atlas proof is unperformed. Its absence alone is not blocking for this code-review verdict, per the brief. Before landing, after the blocking correction:

1. Run the targeted normalization, persistence, identity-install, and new startup conversation regressions on Atlas at the reviewed replacement head. Include record-only and layout-only duplicates, conflicting first/later metadata and conversations, duplicate Codex contexts, and unknown/empty-leaf controls.
2. Launch the actual packaged tagged app in an isolated domain/state folder with the malformed fixture and `C11_QA_LAUNCH=resume`. Show no process death and a working socket; exactly A/B/C once each; left area A/B in order, right area C; selected B/C with global focus C; the first complete A record's content/metadata/conversation retained; B/C content intact. Capture diagnostics naming synthetic A for one dropped record and both dropped layout references. Repeat with agent-bearing duplicate records to exercise the startup crash seam, using synthetic conversation data and controlled test transcripts.
3. Capture a normal session from that running isolated app with terminal, local markdown, and about:blank browser tabs across two areas. Relaunch it and prove UUIDs, types/content, order, area placement/selection, metadata, rail state, and split geometry remain intact. The host mixed-tab test alone does not establish AC2's real-session control.
4. Save the repaired graph through the app's normal persistence, quit cleanly, and relaunch the same tag again. Inspect the saved file and live tree/socket state: one A/B/C, repaired placements/selections, first-record metadata/conversation, no duplicate reintroduction and no crash. Run both phases of `tests_v2/test_duplicate_session_restore.py` for its covered assertions; supplement its metadata-only fixture for startup conversations and visible content.
5. Retain logs, tree/socket evidence, saved snapshot, and screenshots. Enumerate and use a verified display, impose a hard UI-run timeout, confirm readable areas and restored content/selection through computer use, dismiss the tagged app with synthesized input, and prove dismissal. Keep production state untouched.

This reaches the formerly trapping unique-key dictionary.
2. `c11Tests/SessionRestoreNormalizationTests.swift:88` prepares multiple windows/workspaces, checks retained records and diagnostic identities, and verifies repeated preparation/direct normalization yields no drops and identical encoded state.
3. `c11Tests/WorkspaceConversationResumeTests.swift:31` checks conflicting native conversations through the real bridge, store seed, pendingRestartPlans, sessionSnapshot capture, and temporary-file persistence round trip. The asserted resume plan names the first conversation.
4. `c11Tests/WorkspaceConversationResumeTests.swift:35` drives the same executable path when the first record has no conversation. It asserts no adopted later conversation, no resume plan, and no discarded conversation persisted.

# C11-315 validation

## Exact-head Atlas gate

- Branch head: `129bc00875fd7601dc79bf63fd3371310490f633`
- Base: `origin/main` / C11-314 `9f2173320a9dac428edaef1512dc0271b766802a`
- Invocation: `fab9187df3bb4b1eab305d0e4fbd97a1`
- Command: `scripts/remote-build.sh --tag c11-315-final --mode test -- -only-testing:c11LogicTests -skip-testing:c11LogicTests/SocketControlPasswordStoreTests`
- Atlas result: `C11_REMOTE_OK compile=ok tests=ok`
- Result: `c11LogicTests.xctest` passed, 2,376 tests executed, 3 skipped, 0 failures.
- C11-314 seam: `WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests` ran 2 tests and passed; it was not skipped.
- The only skipped class was `SocketControlPasswordStoreTests`, whose SSH path requires Keychain access.
- Atlas toolchain: Xcode 26.3 (17C529), Zig 0.15.2.
- Pinned submodules: Ghostty `5830d1976eecca0d7dee202aef8fb2338d99ed6d`; Bonsplit `c17c6f41cd71066bda9bec82c54465fe34821c75`.
- Remote artifact log: `~/c11-builds/c11-315-final/artifacts/fab9187df3bb4b1eab305d0e4fbd97a1/build.log`.

## Local checks

- `tests/test_ci_schedule_policy.sh` passed.
- `tests/test_ci_self_hosted_guard.sh` passed.
- `tests/test_ci_atlas_tools.sh` passed.
- `tests/test_ci_ghosttykit_checksum_verification.sh` and checksum-present guard passed.
- `tests/drawbridge/test_gates.py`: 40 tests passed.
- YAML parsing, shell syntax, `test_with_build_lock.sh`, create-dmg pinning, scheme TestAction Debug, and GhosttyKit guard passed.
- `tests/test_ci_universal_release_settings.sh` remains a baseline failure because `origin/main` has no `scripts/build-sign-upload.sh`; C11-315 does not touch that release path.

## Atlas runner

- Runner `atlas-c11-315` is online and idle with labels `self-hosted,macOS,ARM64,atlas`.
- It is installed under Atlas `~/c11-actions-runner` and started with `nohup ./run.sh`; no launchd/system install, global Xcode change, or keychain access was used.

## Validator scenario

1. Inspect the merged `main` workflow graph. Expected: `ci.yml` is the pull-request fast lane with only workflow guards, remote-daemon tests, and web typecheck; it has no native build job or push trigger.
2. Dispatch `CI hourly (Atlas)` from internal `main`. Expected: the job claims `self-hosted,macOS,atlas`, and every heavy command logs admission through `scripts/ci-atlas-run.sh` before the c11 build lock.
3. Inspect a fork pull request event. Expected: no Atlas workflow job is eligible because the internal-repository guard rejects cross-repository heads.
4. Inspect the next hourly run after a Ghostty submodule bump. Expected: the GhosttyKit workflow preserves the prerelease artifact and pinned checksum flow, while the hourly main result is the authoritative landing signal.
5. If the hourly main run is red after landing, fix forward on the same mainline rather than treating the already-landed PR as a failed PR gate.

# C11-315 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL**

Head: `129bc00875fd7601dc79bf63fd3371310490f633`.
Base: `9f2173320a9dac428edaef1512dc0271b766802a` (merge-base with freshly fetched `origin/main`).

Reviewed the full 16-file diff and its workflow, runner, admission, checksum, smoke-test, and Drawbridge seams. Detached checkout was clean; the remote PR head still matched at closeout. No builds or tests were run by this reviewer. GitHub reports all three fast PR checks successful. The owner's Atlas logic-test result is recorded evidence, not an independently replayed Actions workflow.

## Blocking

1. **Critical: the registered runner is reachable through attacker-edited fork workflows.** Locations: `.github/workflows/ci-hourly.yml:20-21`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:4`, and the runner registration reported in validation `ev_01M3YMD0AWF4HRBFVX7ETT2FN1`. Live read-only inspection found `atlas-c11-315` online with the self-hosted/macOS/atlas labels, registered directly to this public repository in the Default pool; its listener runs as the operator's account. The repository's fork-contributor approval policy is `first_time_contributors`. A returning external contributor can change the existing PR workflow to request those runner labels and execute arbitrary steps. They can also change/remove a YAML `if`; the three guards in this branch cannot enforce runner access against a PR that supplies its own workflow. This violates the explicit no-fork-execution acceptance criterion and exposes the runner account's accessible state, even though GitHub withholds repository secrets from ordinary fork jobs. Smallest safe containment: take this repository-scoped runner out of service, then route the trusted internal workflows through an independently enforced runner-access boundary (for example a private CI repository, or an available workflow/ref-restricted runner group). Prove the server-side restriction, not merely the unchanged YAML guard. [GitHub's runner-access documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-runners/self-hosted-runners/manage-access) explicitly describes the public-fork execution risk. No exploit was submitted and no runner configuration was changed during review.

2. **High: compatibility CI exits before its Xcode fallback on Atlas.** Location: `.github/workflows/ci-macos-compat.yml:40-45`. Read-only Atlas enumeration found `Xcode.app` and `Xcode-26.3.app`, with no `Xcode_*.app`. The `ls` assignment therefore returns nonzero under `set -euo pipefail`, so the shell exits before reaching the fallback to `Xcode.app`. Moving this previously hosted job onto Atlas makes every compatibility run fail at Select Xcode. Smallest fix: use the checked `Xcode.app`/`Xcode*.app` discovery already used by the other native workflows, including a nonfatal no-match branch. Exercise that selection in the actual Actions environment.

3. **High: the documented landing gate omits native validation for ordinary Swift changes.** Locations: `CLAUDE.md:132-134`, `skills/lattice-orchestrator/references/orchestrator.md:149-151`, and `skills/c11-hotload/SKILL.md:32-35`. The new instructions require Atlas only when CI/build tooling changes. A source-only Swift PR can consequently land with review plus Ubuntu checks, even if it does not compile; the removed PR build no longer catches it. This contradicts this ticket's prescribed landing gate of Atlas exact-head validation. Smallest fix: make the Atlas gate the replacement native landing gate for applicable code changes, preserving explicitly justified documentation-only exemptions and the Ghostty checksum exception. Keep hourly red-main handling as fix-forward.

4. **Medium: a paid native PR/push lane remains active.** Locations: `CLAUDE.md:116-121` and the unchanged interacting `.github/workflows/mailbox-parity.yml:25-47,69-73`. A PR or push changing `CLI/c11.swift`, mailbox sources, wrappers, or the listed tests still schedules `mailbox-unit` on `macos-15-xlarge` and invokes the native logic build/test path. Thus the claimed cheap-only PR lane and absence of push-triggered native CI are false for common source changes. Smallest fix: move the native mailbox coverage into the scheduled/manual lane (the hourly full logic suite already includes mailbox logic), retaining cheap checks on PRs as needed.

5. **Medium: the documented Ghostty bump sequence cannot clear the pre-merge checksum gate.** Locations: `.github/workflows/build-ghosttykit.yml:3-6`, `CLAUDE.md:268-274`, and Validator scenario 4 in `ev_01M3YMF84Y5N43N9C5YBQH7TWF`. For a PR that introduces a new Ghostty SHA, `ci.yml:52-53` still fails until the checksum exists, but the producer no longer runs on PRs. Waiting for the documented hourly main producer cannot repair that unmerged branch; main still contains the old SHA. Manual dispatch on the internal bump branch is available, but the new guidance and scenario only describe a post-merge main checksum window. Smallest fix: explicitly require trusted manual dispatch against the bump branch before landing, wait for its checksum commit, and obtain fresh checks/review at the resulting head. Replace the post-merge-only scenario with this pre-merge round trip, including how the required PR checks are started after the bot commit. No need to restore automatic native work on every PR.

6. **Medium: the new schedule test violates the explicit test-quality policy.** Location: `tests/test_ci_schedule_policy.sh:19-46`, invoked by `.github/workflows/ci.yml:25-26`. Every assertion greps checked-in YAML or Markdown for implementation text; no assertion exercises scheduling or runner eligibility. This is precisely the source/metadata-only test form prohibited by `CLAUDE.md` and the reviewer contract. Its green result also misses the remaining mailbox lane in finding 4. Smallest fix: remove the new source-only test and its CI invocation, or replace it with genuine execution/eligibility evidence through a meaningful harness. Keep the behavioral admission helper test. Do not describe grep assertions as behavioral coverage.

## Non-blocking

None. The changed heavy xcodebuild/Zig calls correctly use the existing two-slot scheduler and nested build lock. The current Drawbridge workflows remain on Ubuntu and their gate still consumes the configured required-check list. `release.yml` is unchanged and still selects a hosted runner label absent from Atlas. Ghostty artifact publishing retains both `--prerelease` and `--latest=false`; no Sparkle feed path was changed.

## Runtime proof still required

The supplied numbered Validator scenario is inadequate for runner access and pre-merge checksum production, as detailed above. Amend it to cover:

1. Independently enforced denial of fork-controlled workflows, including an edited runner request from a returning contributor; confirm only the permitted internal workflows/refs can target Atlas and release workflows cannot. Use safe validation after containment, with no untrusted execution on the operator account.
2. Successful actual Actions runs of hourly build/logic, compatibility, and GhosttyKit paths on Atlas, including Xcode discovery, slot/build-lock admission alongside the existing remote route, and smoke completion/cleanup. The owner's SSH remote-build result does not exercise those YAML steps.
3. A new Ghostty SHA on an internal branch completing manual artifact publication, checksum commit, fresh required PR checks, and exact-head landing validation before merge. Confirm the artifact remains a prerelease and does not take the latest release slot.
4. A mailbox/CLI change scheduling only cheap PR checks, followed by its native coverage in the scheduled/manual lane.

Per the batch-validation contract, deferred runtime proof alone is not the reason for FAIL. The concrete security, execution, acceptance, documentation, and test-policy defects above are blocking. Security containment is needed now because the runner is already online, independently of whether this PR lands.
Atin (2026-10-02): approved hosted hourly CI only for 1.0; no self-hosted runner in this ticket; revisit an Atlas runner after the run (no outside contributors today).

C11-273.title: Implement journal append, SQLite store, pure fold and bounded replay

data.from:
## Why
A finished agent must not return to working because an earlier hook arrived late, and a crash must not erase the evidence of an unresolved ask. The same record must support the operator’s analytics questions. Backlog item: J2.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:426` handles report_agent_activity off-main and hops to main at `:437`; `Sources/TabLivenessDeriver.swift:155` writes derived activity. `Sources/Events/EventLog.swift:51` and `:70` show why the lossy telemetry log cannot be the durable journal. `Sources/AgentModelDetection.swift:2` already imports SQLite3.
- Upstream: #10490; `Packages/macOS/CmuxAgentJournal/Sources/CmuxAgentJournal/AgentJournalStore.swift:78` stable-id append receipts; `AgentLifecycleReducer.swift:62` ordering and `AgentJournalReplayPolicy.swift:24` replay filtering. #15173/#16257 motivate late-arrival fixtures.
- Research: BACKLOG.md J2; report 01 Components/Effort and risk; Astra §4 spool/retention counterexamples; J1’s reviewed spec. The 2026-10-01 BACKLOG.md rulings D1/D3 override the older audit and c11-1.0.html deferral: the journal is core 1.0, uses SQLite WAL, and has analytics as its named consumer.

## Scope
In: agent.event.append, system SQLite WAL under c11 App Support, serial storage, pure fold, current-state baseline, client spool/startup drain, time/byte retention, and migration of existing signals into the approved schema. Out: producer widening (J3–J5), roster/clock UI (J6), analytics CLI (J7), Feed replies, auto-resume, remote federation and tenant hooks installation.

## Approach
Implement the reviewed J1 schema and bounds. Parse/validate/attribute off main, serialize durable writes, return the defined receipt, and apply only the changed projection using main.async. Map existing Claude/OpenCode/pi and guarded Codex-notify inputs without changing their authority or double-counting. Reuse existing exact conversation identity. Retain activity compatibility and keep the telemetry log a separate wake-up stream. Use stable event IDs for ambiguous acknowledgements; startup drains only bounded c11-owned spool records with known attribution.

## Acceptance criteria
1. F3 replays yield their approved marks: bypass asks remain blocked, Stop then late earlier PreToolUse stays completed, Esc is not asserted working after its supported interrupt signal, sibling activity cannot clear another ask, and child completion cannot finish its parent.
2. Against a tagged socket, append returns the committed sequence per J1. Repeating a timed-out committed record from the spool yields one event and the original receipt; a same-ID/different-content retry reports conflict without replacing it.
3. With the app socket unavailable, the client records a bounded c11-owned spool entry; after startup it drains once. Exercise a truncated last line, stale session/tab attribution and a repeated drain using the J1 outcomes.
4. Force-kill/relaunch of the tagged app shows prior blocked/error evidence as unconfirmed, never old running as present liveness; fresh supported events reconcile it. A retained old open ask survives the time/byte pruning fixture.
5. During the F3 burst and F2 registered workload, append/fold I/O does not block main and resource/typing measurements remain within registered budgets; saturation/disk failure exposes degraded evidence per spec.
6. The existing sidebar, ⌥V and flag/suppression workflows still consume activity as specified. Journal, WAL, spool and error paths contain only allowlisted structural fields, with no prompt/tool bodies.

## Validation
Execute pure fold and SQLite behavioral tests with a temporary database and F3 replay; exercise retry/drain/restart via tests_v2 against an isolated tagged socket. Independently view blocked/unread/replay marks with computer use on a verified display, timeout and dismissal. Native builds, full tests and F2 soak run on Atlas after C11-216; do not equate build-for-testing with assertions.

## Dependencies
Depends on J1; F3 and F1 / C11-216 are transitive. Coordinates the single blocked-state contract with A2 (Feed) and A1 scoped fixes; those cross-workstream links are for the lead. J3–J7 depend on this seam. J8 documents and syncs new verbs.

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: L. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.

# C11-273 validation checkpoint

Implementation is pushed on `c11-1.0/C11-273-journal`. This checkpoint is not a performance PASS or a review handoff.

## Artifact and scope

The tagged Debug artifact has product source commit `52056252f3f30b3bf42af24fd1c69b5ab724bf0c`, based on main `43529df178a9cd8817fc092896efd2f3fcd63df5`, including C11-263 `6926fa05cf`. Later commits through `e764720703` change tests and probes only. The executable hash in the manifest distinguishes the remote build from the retrieved, path-adjusted signed artifact used in the guest.

All packaged-app execution used a disposable guest, a tagged app, an explicit isolated socket and QA fresh/resume. The real hooks, socket, SQLite files, spool, terminal and UI were exercised. Provider inputs were synthetic structural events except the explicitly recorded C11-271 hook shape. This does not claim a live provider end-to-end run or unsupported interrupt coverage.

## Passed checks

- **25 journal logic tests**: reducer 9, store 11, spool 5; invocation `60875ef7f7a5431e8e4fd905577fd8e7`. Actual test action passed, including reopening the database and folding multiple historical events after the process changes. Prior targeted liveness/journal gate passed 45 tests before that additional store test. Four workspace-constructing liveness tests were excluded for the known no-host NSApp limitation. The two run-wide test exclusions were also applied.
- **Three guest runtime scripts**: `test_journal_append_replay.py`, `test_journal_restart.py`, and the unchanged `test_claude_attention_batch.py` passed. See [runtime-checks.txt](runtime-checks.txt). They cover sibling/seen/legacy isolation, blocked persistence across Stop/late tools, terminal ordering, recorded ExitPlanMode input, lost reply retry and conflicting draft rejection, child/stale ownership, structural privacy, crash/reopen and repeat drain. Offline append/spool took 13.6 ms in this run.
- **Real UI**: [report](journal-ui/report.json), 12.105 seconds. Journal-only attention enables the actual Jump menu without routine unread; actual key/menu navigation selects it; seeing does not resolve it; suppression excludes routine waiting and a flag retains precedence. A forced restart exposes Unconfirmed in actual accessibility help. Synthesized dismissal and readable one-area topology passed.
- **Compatibility**: packaged CLI transport/authentication checks, mailbox hook drain checks, five bounded transcript tests, and the OpenCode lifecycle test passed during implementation. They were not repeated as full suites after test-only edits.

The UI run uses an ordinary per-tag user shortcut binding for Option-V to exercise the spec's named gesture. The current shipped default is Control-Command-Return. Screenshots have neutral prompts and are cropped to the app/menu. No tenant tool configuration was written.

## Performance and remaining work

The required short matched comparison is **incomplete**. An early baseline probe failed glyph matching under hook traffic; it provides no valid candidate-versus-baseline latency conclusion. A later setup attempt found no window after launching the baseline; the runner now explicitly creates a window when needed. Failed samples are not represented as zero latency or a pass. The prior guest was deleted at the lease boundary.

The bounded final comparison uses the same 120 real key-to-glyph trials, eight structural hook producers, geometry and capture method on both artifacts. It records p95/p99, capture overhead, hook timing, CPU, RSS, physical footprint and host/guest load. The pre-registered C11-270 comparison thresholds are p95 `max(baseline * 1.20, baseline + 5 ms)`, p99 `max(baseline * 1.25, baseline + 15 ms)`, and peak footprint `max(baseline * 1.25, baseline + 2048 MiB)`. More than 5% unmatched glyphs invalidates the measurement. This short run cannot establish a fleet-soak memory slope or main-thread stall distribution.

A final committed-head Debug build, bounded comparison, durable results, draft PR and orchestrator-owned Fable review remain. No PR has been opened and no merge is authorized for this owner.

Expect journal-only Jump, suppression/flag precedence, persistent blocked state after seeing, and Unconfirmed after force-kill/resume. Expect `cleanup_ok: true` and inspect the cropped screenshots.
3. Run the same `journal_perf_probe.py` on a tagged main baseline and candidate under matching geometry and load. Retain calibration/miss counts and compare only valid samples using the registered thresholds. Report short-run scope separately from the deferred fleet soak.
4. Delete the run's guest and tag caches after retaining sanitized evidence. The merge owner syncs installed skill copies from merged main.

## Verdict: FAIL

The store, fold, spool and socket seam are sound and match the spec's mechanism (one writer queue, one pure fold, one bounded spool, no epochs or markers). The failures are in the compatibility bridge: the journal's blocked state now drives the sidebar mark and ⌥V, but for Claude Code and OpenCode nothing in this PR can ever resolve a blocked ask except the next prompt. That turns a correct "unanswered ask stays blocked" rule into a visible regression on the most common flow (answer or approve, agent continues). Two smaller compatibility regressions ride along.

## Blocking

### 1. Answered asks and approved permissions stay painted `waiting` until the next prompt

- `CLI/JournalCommand.swift:150-190` (`claudeDraft`): maps PreToolUse AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode to `question/plan_review.requested` and Notification `permission_prompt` to `approval.requested` (with `request_id = nil`). There is no `post-tool-use` case and no mapping that emits `agent.attention.resolved`. `Resources/bin/claude:239` subscribes no PostToolUse or PermissionRequest hook.
- `Sources/Journal/JournalReducer.swift:135-140, 148-150`: while `phase == .blocked`, `tool_activity` is `advisory` and `turn.completed` is `advisory`; only `turn.started` with `UserPromptSubmit`/`chat.message` or a correlated `attention.resolved` leaves blocked.
- `Sources/TabLivenessDeriver.swift:11-15` and `Sources/Workspace.swift:6675`: `hasJournalAttention` (phase blocked or error) forces `.waiting`; `Sources/TabLivenessDeriver.swift:137, 178, 300` suppress every legacy derived writer for the tab while a journal snapshot exists, so the old PreToolUse→working path cannot correct it. `Sources/AppDelegate.swift:10861-10890` enables Jump and routes ⌥V to these tabs first.

Failure scenario (normal permission mode, every session): PreToolUse(Bash) → Notification `permission_prompt` → journal `blocked/approval`. Operator approves; Bash runs; the next PreToolUse folds `advisory("tool_cannot_start_turn")`; Stop folds `advisory("unresolved_request")`. The tab stays `.waiting`, Jump is enabled, ⌥V jumps there, and the tooltip says "Approval" through the rest of the turn and after completion, until the operator types the next prompt. On main the tab-scoped PreToolUse clear plus `report_agent_activity working` returned the mark to running within one hook. The same happens for a bypass AskUserQuestion after the operator answers (the C11-271 Q2 oracle is "bypass ask + seen + response + resumed"), for ExitPlanMode after plan approval, and for OpenCode `permission.asked` after the reply (`skills/opencode-plugins/c11-notify.js:139`, no `permission.replied` mapping).

The evidence does not cover this path. `c11Tests/Fixtures/lifecycle/normalized/claude-bypass-ask.json` ends at the unanswered ask (seq 8). `tests_v2/test_journal_append_replay.py:66-73` sends PreToolUse(Bash) then Stop after the ask and asserts `blocked`, labelled "late tool/Stop", but that is byte-for-byte the trace of an answered ask, so the test enshrines the regression rather than guarding against it. The UI probe checks "seeing does not resolve" and never answers an ask.

Smallest fix (two parts, both inside the attested semantics; part a touches a hook subscription that the plan assigned to C11-274, so the Orchestrator should attest it here or hold the merge until that producer lands):

a. Subscribe `PostToolUse` with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode` in `Resources/bin/claude` and add a `post-tool-use` case to `claudeDraft` emitting `agent.attention.resolved{resolution: resumed, request_id: tool_use_id, turn_id: prompt_id}`. The reducer already correlates it (`JournalReducer.swift:142-147`). This is exact and clears the mark the moment the ask returns.

b. For approvals, which carry no request ID: in the Claude adapter path only, treat a hook-rank `turn.completed` whose `turn_id` equals the blocked snapshot's `turn_id` as resolution of that turn's request (Claude Code cannot emit Stop while a permission prompt is pending, so same-turn Stop is the spec's "verified continuation of that turn"). This is a one-guard change in the `.turnCompleted` case and needs a sentence-level spec attestation, not new mechanism.

Then extend `claude-bypass-ask` (or add the answered variant) with answer → PreToolUse → Stop and assert the mark returns to idle, and change the replay script's "late tool/Stop" assertion to use a *different* turn ID so it tests lateness rather than continuation.

### 2. Ordinary PreToolUse no longer updates the Claude status pill

- `CLI/c11.swift:17737-17741`: after `clear_notifications`, `if appendJournal(...) { print("OK"); return }` was inserted *before* the `setClaudeStatus(... "Running" / verbose tool status ...)` block that follows at `:17749-17760`. Only the legacy `reportAgentActivity` was meant to be skipped; the status write went with it.

Failure scenario: Notification `permission_prompt` sets status "Needs input" (`:17587`). Operator approves; Claude runs ten more tools; the sidebar status stays "Needs input" until Stop writes "Idle" (`:17497`). With `claudeCodeVerboseStatus` on, per-tool status never updates. On main each ordinary PreToolUse wrote "Running" or the tool description. `prompt-submit` and `stop` still set their statuses, so this is specific to the resume-after-prompt path, which is exactly the path the comment at `:17683` says this case exists for.

Smallest fix: keep the early return only around the legacy `reportAgentActivity(working)` call and let the `setClaudeStatus` block run regardless of journal delivery.

### 3. Legacy liveness writers stay suppressed after the agent session ends

- `Sources/TabLivenessDeriver.swift:137, 155, 178-190, 213, 300, 364, 396, 433`: every legacy path (`report_agent_activity`, Return-key submit, notification-store idle, the 10 s reconcile) returns early whenever `JournalCoordinator.shared.snapshot(tabID:) != nil`, regardless of the snapshot's `connection`.
- `CLI/c11.swift:17654-17662`: session-end pushes the same ref with `state: "ended"`; `Sources/Conversation/Ref.swift:171` keeps it an eligible causal owner, so `Store.swift:267-274` does not change the owner and the coordinator keeps the `sessionEnded` snapshot (disconnected, unconfirmed) for the tab indefinitely. The snapshot is only dropped on owner change or tab close (`JournalCoordinator.swift:21-35`).

Failure scenario: Claude exits in a tab (SessionEnd). The operator runs a long shell command or launches an unmanaged agent that reports through `c11 agent-hook working|idle` (pi with no captured conversation, or any v1 reporter). Those writes are dropped and the reconcile sweep skips the tab, so the sidebar shows no activity for that tab until a new conversation ref is captured or the tab is closed. Spec §5: "shells and unmanaged sessions retain their existing fallback"; plan §5 scopes suppression to "a journal-managed owner". An ended session is not a managed owner.

Smallest fix: gate suppression on a live projection, e.g. `snapshot?.connection == .live` (or `!isHistorical`), in the deriver guards and `applyToStore`. Historical blocked/error evidence keeps painting through `journalByTab` and the attention resolver; it just stops vetoing legacy writers. `Workspace.restoreSessionSnapshot` already clears stale derived working on restore, so nothing else changes.

## Non-blocking

4. **Startup drain spins at 10 Hz on persistent storage failure.** `JournalCoordinator.swift:143-151` reschedules every 100 ms while `remaining`; `JournalSpool.swift:120-128` sets `remaining` for any non-permanent error (`busy`, `full`, `unavailable`). With the database at its byte cap, each tick lists the spool, claims a file, runs the pressure prune transaction and checkpoint, fails, and renames back, indefinitely. Off main, but it is a constant CPU/IO load on exactly the degraded machine. Back off (stop after N consecutive failed batches or use an exponential delay) and let the next startup retry.
5. **Normal-mode AskUserQuestion is double-counted as approval.** PreToolUse gives `question/request tool-1`; the following Notification `permission_prompt` gives `approval/request nil`; the reducer's duplicate check compares request IDs (`JournalReducer.swift:128`) so it applies, flips the reason to approval and resets `since`. Q3 grouping and wait duration drift. Treat a permission Notification arriving while blocked by a hook-rank question/plan of the same turn as `duplicate_evidence`.
6. **`working` rows are protected from baseline pruning forever.** `JournalStore.swift:163` marks `paintsAttention || phase == .working` protected; `pruneOnQueue` only evicts unprotected rows. A session that dies mid-turn leaves a permanent row; over months this fills the 16 MiB current-state budget and new owners get `journal_full`. Spec protects only open blocked/error. Make `protected = paintsAttention`.
7. **Hook delivery budget is 250 ms twice, not 250 ms total.** `CLI/c11.swift:2012-2014` caps connect at 250 ms and `JournalCommand.deliver` caps the append at another 250 ms, then the remaining v1 calls run on their normal timeouts. Spec says 250 ms total. Acceptable for now, but say so in `skills/c11/references/api.md`.
8. **Every append retries a full open while storage is failing.** `JournalCoordinator.storage()` reruns `prepare()`, SQLite open, PRAGMAs and the prune on each hook event when `store == nil`. Bounded, but consider remembering the failure for a few seconds.
9. **Validation README is stale** on "No PR or HANDOFF" (superseded by the handoff comment). Update when the fix lands.
10. **Fixture replay** (`JournalReducerTests.swift:139-165`) covers two of twelve normalized fixtures and only their claude-hook rows. Fine for this ticket; the answered-ask variant from Blocking 1 is the one to add.

# C11-284 bundle identity diagnosis and runtime checks

Needs operator: nothing. Offline and live runtime PASS on the exact candidate. Nullable commit remains unknown; version/build supplies the permitted build stamp identity.

Candidate: merged head `b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35`, canonical invocation `273d23384a7a436b8d5d14b81eb6f292`, clean source/empty overlay. Build-host executable SHA256 `4f964b60873ddb4dfae4153ea2e1308605ba0995480acb344e2614e3fc6524ac`; separately signed interactive-session/guest copy SHA256 `25be5130f86178e852a6da28b05966ab9c750bf48ab3c76a86c417d7807115fc`.

## Finding: pre-existing stamp phase can run too early

The build-host's actual current `$HOME`-owned tag build log (`/tmp/c11-xcodebuild-val-3.log`) places app `PhaseScriptExecution Run Script` at line 233, then app `ProcessInfoPlistFile` at line 810. The script stamps `${TARGET_BUILD_DIR}/${INFOPLIST_PATH}` only when the file already exists. Xcode subsequently generates the product Info.plist from `Resources/Info.plist`, which contains no C11Commit/CMUXCommit. Thus a fresh product can skip stamping, and an existing stamped product can be overwritten by the later plist task. The final packaged Info.plist indeed contains version `0.67.0`, build `131`, and neither commit key.

This is an actual packaging ordering weakness, not evidence that Debug intentionally never stamps. The existing stamp block has no Debug exemption. Git history places the C11Commit phase under earlier branding commit `6d0bc1a843` (#37), before C11-284. `scripts/reload.sh` retags/re-signs after xcodebuild and does not re-add C11Commit; the nightly workflow independently stamps both commit keys after building. No build, plist edit, new stamp, source change or signing change was performed for this diagnosis.

## Contract: nullable commit is represented honestly

C11-284's ticket explicitly accepts version plus git SHA **or build stamp**. `Sources/BundledSkill.swift:3` confines identity to the built bundle, models commit as optional, prints version/build even without a commit, and returns unknown (`nil`/JSON null) from commitsMatch when either commit is unavailable or malformed. CLI capabilities help at `CLI/c11.swift:8684` says sha_match is null when either build lacks a stamp. This runtime supports an unstamped bundle honestly; that fallback does not imply the packaging ordering weakness is desirable.

The stock `tests_v2/test_guide_and_features.py:83` imposes a stricter non-null commit assertion, then its synthetic-case construction calls `.startswith` on that assumed non-null value. That fixture rejects a permitted build-stamp identity. The ignored `C11-284-nullable-runtime.py` changes only the fixture assumptions: require version/build and its printed header; retain actual commit null; compare null/missing/valid/invalid/empty synthetic peer commits with the expected unknown result. C11-277.title: Query lifecycle analytics and export the journal as NDJSON

data.from:
## Why
The operator explicitly wants to know where agent time goes, which waits cost attention and which sessions stall. Durable history earns its place by answering those questions for dashboards and humans. Backlog item: J7.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Sources/AgentLaunchStats.swift:5` records launches and `:130` aggregates harness/model/provider counts; that is not lifecycle dwell, blocked time or response latency. `Sources/Events/EventLog.swift:51` and `:70` bound/drop the current telemetry history.
- Upstream: #10490 journal query substrate, `Packages/macOS/CmuxAgentJournal/Sources/CmuxAgentJournal/AgentJournalStore.swift:78`. Do not import unrelated upstream messaging/auto-resume policy.
- Research: BACKLOG.md J7 and explicit D1 analytics ruling; report 01 What the journal unlocks; Astra §4 query/dedupe/retention and §7 privacy budgets. The 2026-10-01 BACKLOG.md rulings D1/D3 override the older audit and c11-1.0.html deferral: the journal is core 1.0, uses SQLite WAL, and has analytics as its named consumer.

## Scope
In: c11 stats or c11 journal query (choose a documented nonconflicting CLI shape), filters by agent/model/workspace/time, JSON and readable reports, six named metrics and NDJSON export. Out: a hosted dashboard, provider billing/token pricing, replacing C11-178 launch-count stats, autonomous stall intervention, automatic flag raising and focus-history tracking.

## Approach
Query J2’s SQLite off main using bounded windows/indexes and the J1 interval/coverage contract. Keep closed intervals separate from ongoing waits, report left/right-censored or missing intervals, and do not count restored unconfirmed time as verified agent work. Define operator-response latency from supported response/resolution evidence, not merely viewing a tab. Use structural/model/workspace attribution captured at the event time; distinguish unknown values. Export ordered stable IDs and source/coverage metadata without bodies.

## Acceptance criteria
1. For a deterministic multi-agent/model/workspace timeline, JSON and readable output answer time in each state, wait-to-operator-response, blocked minutes, turns per hour, errors/interrupts and stall outliers, with explicitly documented units and denominators.
2. Filter each dimension and a clipped time window against known interval totals. A wait begun before the window contributes only its overlap; a still-open wait is labeled ongoing rather than a completed response.
3. The F3 seen-but-not-answered and late-hook cases do not undercount blocked minutes or manufacture a response. Hook-plus-transcript duplicates do not inflate turns; disconnected/gap/unconfirmed ranges expose incomplete coverage.
4. NDJSON export is parseable, ordered and repeatable for a fixed journal snapshot, includes event IDs/provenance, and contains no prompt/tool bodies. A small dashboard-reader example can consume JSON without scraping human text.
5. At the registered F2 event volume, queries and export stay within the J1 time/memory bounds without stalling append or UI typing; retention-limited results disclose the retained coverage window.

## Validation
Use SQLite fixture timelines with independently calculated totals, including open waits, interrupted turns, duplicate delivery, source changes and retention boundaries. Exercise the actual CLI against a tagged socket/store and parse JSON/NDJSON with a sample consumer. No dashboard UI is required; observe typing during analytics/export in the Atlas fleet soak. Native builds/full tests/soaks run on Atlas after C11-216.

## Dependencies
Depends on J2 and the J1 data/interval contract. Coordinate snapshot reason/source fields with J6, but J6 is not a hard dependency on the query engine. C11-178 remains launch statistics; do not duplicate or overwrite it. J8 documents the chosen verbs.

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.

## Why
The operator explicitly wants to know where agent time goes, which waits cost attention and which sessions stall. Durable history earns its place by answering those questions for dashboards and humans. Backlog item: J7.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Sources/AgentLaunchStats.swift:5` records launches and `:130` aggregates harness/model/provider counts; that is not lifecycle dwell, blocked time or response latency. `Sources/Events/EventLog.swift:51` and `:70` bound/drop the current telemetry history.
- Upstream: #10490 journal query substrate, `Packages/macOS/CmuxAgentJournal/Sources/CmuxAgentJournal/AgentJournalStore.swift:78`. Do not import unrelated upstream messaging/auto-resume policy.
- Research: BACKLOG.md J7 and explicit D1 analytics ruling; report 01 What the journal unlocks; Astra §4 query/dedupe/retention and §7 privacy budgets. The 2026-10-01 BACKLOG.md rulings D1/D3 override the older audit and c11-1.0.html deferral: the journal is core 1.0, uses SQLite WAL, and has analytics as its named consumer.

## Scope
In: c11 stats or c11 journal query (choose a documented nonconflicting CLI shape), filters by agent/model/workspace/time, JSON and readable reports, six named metrics and NDJSON export. Out: a hosted dashboard, provider billing/token pricing, replacing C11-178 launch-count stats, autonomous stall intervention, automatic flag raising and focus-history tracking.

## Approach
Query J2’s SQLite off main using bounded windows/indexes and the J1 interval/coverage contract. Keep closed intervals separate from ongoing waits, report left/right-censored or missing intervals, and do not count restored unconfirmed time as verified agent work. Define operator-response latency from supported response/resolution evidence, not merely viewing a tab. Use structural/model/workspace attribution captured at the event time; distinguish unknown values. Export ordered stable IDs and source/coverage metadata without bodies.

## Acceptance criteria
1. For a deterministic multi-agent/model/workspace timeline, JSON and readable output answer time in each state, wait-to-operator-response, blocked minutes, turns per hour, errors/interrupts and stall outliers, with explicitly documented units and denominators.
2. Filter each dimension and a clipped time window against known interval totals. A wait begun before the window contributes only its overlap; a still-open wait is labeled ongoing rather than a completed response.
3. The F3 seen-but-not-answered and late-hook cases do not undercount blocked minutes or manufacture a response. Hook-plus-transcript duplicates do not inflate turns; disconnected/gap/unconfirmed ranges expose incomplete coverage.
4. NDJSON export is parseable, ordered and repeatable for a fixed journal snapshot, includes event IDs/provenance, and contains no prompt/tool bodies. A small dashboard-reader example can consume JSON without scraping human text.
5. At the registered F2 event volume, queries and export stay within the J1 time/memory bounds without stalling append or UI typing; retention-limited results disclose the retained coverage window.

## Validation
Use SQLite fixture timelines with independently calculated totals, including open waits, interrupted turns, duplicate delivery, source changes and retention boundaries. Exercise the actual CLI against a tagged socket/store and parse JSON/NDJSON with a sample consumer. No dashboard UI is required; observe typing during analytics/export in the Atlas fleet soak. Native builds/full tests/soaks run on Atlas after C11-216.

## Dependencies
Depends on J2 and the J1 data/interval contract. Coordinate snapshot reason/source fields with J6, but J6 is not a hard dependency on the query engine. C11-178 remains launch statistics; do not duplicate or overwrite it. J8 documents the chosen verbs.
Within-workstream prerequisites: J2 (C11-273).

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.

C11-282.title: Read a terminal selection off the main thread

data.body: Moving scrollback read_text and read-screen off the main actor is C11-295 (ledger B086), after C11-296 teaches that read to start a cold terminal. This ticket stays selection-only. Do not format scrollback here.

# C11-282 validation

Head: `790c98459b836dc754176fc22260ae0f8b40e14b`. Clean, pushed branch `c11-1.0/C11-282-read-selection`. Ordinary merge of main `3786513d84b0d82c2669b2b1b066c54f0d7ada40`: union routing/send/RPC/selection registry entries and preserve both routing and selection documentation sections.

Adds `read-selection` / `tab.read_selection`, terminal-only results, own-tab targeting, explicit-target errors, typed renderer BUSY and `read_selection.terminal` v1. Main resolves the live surface, tries the renderer lock once, copies at most 1 MiB and frees each successful native allocation. Worker clips UTF-8 and constructs text/base64. One monotonic five-second caller deadline includes queueing, capture and encoding; abandoned queued capture is skipped and running capture cleans up without publishing late results. Native formatting/allocation remains synchronous on main and unbounded. The caller deadline and response cap do not bound native work. Root Swift bridge declarations were restored to match C11-294's already-merged native ABI; no engine/submodule edit.

## Checks and identities
- Actual Atlas test action `b7cb5ec3b32c496b842b2071d01aae3a`, clean merge head `b30ce99a17dc5b71e40a8ff5fa5544b51f51976c`: ten tests passed, SelectionReadTests + CapabilityFeaturesTests. Includes actual default five-second abandonment, late running-capture cleanup, one-shot completion, encoding deadline, worker/alias dispatch and UTF-8 below/exact/over-limit boundaries with two/three/four-byte scalars.
- Atlas Debug `5fc36d9e4e504699b135aba96c76b1fb` built and launched that same clean merge head. Subsequent head changes are confined to `tests_v2/test_read_selection.py`; product/test Swift and compiled artifact are unchanged. Captain requires CI green at final head before landing.
- Ghostty `5830d1976eecca0d7dee202aef8fb2338d99ed6d`; Bonsplit `c17c6f41cd71066bda9bec82c54465fe34821c75`.
- Original artifact SHA-256: executable `3abe187162f5fe6341f1a7e0b812b0f7f50bb3769ffba4ce5f007dcac343e1d2`; dylib `5cd35cda888f80bd58b63147f00c6110c5046b7bfae6dc3dd4d0f9e5295775e5`; CLI `a0a77d0e1a5be7612703ed56f2c98932f2a30ca64ad9fa2bc59e5cfacc75a325`. Original artifacts retained privately before remote cache removal.

## Native/runtime evidence
Pre-merge tagged artifact: twenty real mouse select/read/read/built-CLI/clear cycles returned exactly SELECTIONFIXTURE, preserved the selection across reads and stayed alive. No selection, CLI human output/errors, empty/stale window/workspace/tab targets, browser/markdown rejection and hidden legacy alias passed. Browser getSelection call counter remained zero. Final merged artifact: no-selection/discovery plus thirty large native selection reads and built-CLI JSON text/base64 byte parity passed, with no selection mutation. A typed BUSY response was observed during an earlier streaming fixture; the thirty settled samples below all succeeded.

Baseline source `2496017a28e1066a93edb3ad933aa32fe7f62ff6`, Debug `dab6d2cb1ffd43c980040c2618ff2dd3`; same native engine, guest, display, window dimensions and numbered Unicode workload. Both apps used an isolated 50 MB scrollback config. The actually retained selection was 1,045,175 bytes on both artifacts. It remains below the 1 MiB response cap, so these runtime samples report truncated:false. Several-MiB native capture and runtime clipping above the cap are NOT proven; clipping is exercised through the executable logic tests.

All times below are milliseconds, nearest-rank percentiles.

| Path | n | p50 | p95 | p99/max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline native copy caller | 20 | 222.681 | 242.075 | 249.315 |
| Candidate native copy caller | 20 | 228.946 | 254.595 | 271.841 |
| Selection socket caller | 30 | 54.808 | 57.209 | 102.186 |
| Main queue delay | 30 | 0.023 | 0.056 | 47.555 |
| Native formatting on main | 30 | 5.016 | 6.084 | 6.372 |
| Main copy/free | 30 | 0.176 | 0.207 | 0.322 |
| Worker UTF-8/text/base64 | 30 | 1.261 | 1.325 | 1.429 |

DEBUG worker diagnostics show isMain=false. Native timing includes try-lock and formatting together; no separate lock/format estimate is invented. UI-copy timings include driver and pasteboard overhead. Using published C11-270 budget-2 envelopes, the preliminary copy comparison stays below p95 max(baseline*1.2, baseline+5)=290.490 ms and p99 max(baseline*1.25, baseline+15)=311.644 ms. This is not a registered typing/switch soak pass. Typing/switch latency, allocation/leak soak, forced native mutex ownership accounting and a live app-main stall remain integrated-validator work. Production deadline seam tests pass; attempted debugger-based app-main stall was not performed because noninteractive debug attachment was denied. No unbounded native-read claim.

UI ran only in disposable guests: verified native PID/window/display, neutral prompt, exact-window captures, bounded fixture duration, synthesized quit plus confirmation and process disappearance. Both own guests deleted within their leases. Own host tagged app stopped; own remote tag/DerivedData caches removed after retaining artifacts. No installed-skill sync. C11-291 owns translations of admitted English keys.

## Validator scenario
1. Build merged main as a tagged artifact in an isolated guest. Discover terminal selection v1; create a neutral full-size terminal fixture with the committed harness setup phase.
2. Drag the known word using screenshot-derived window-local coordinates; run word and boundaries phases. Expect twenty byte-exact read/read/CLI/clear cycles, no selection success, target errors, unsupported-tab errors and zero browser selection-script calls.
3. Run large phase on actual native scrollback; compare built CLI JSON and base64 byte-exactly. Record the retained native size and truncation. Increase retained native selection beyond 1 MiB for the remaining native clipping proof; do not treat a printed workload size as selected bytes.
4. Measure native main-time and worker timing separately, plus typing/switch latency against the final published C11-270 baseline. Validate forced contention/close-churn and long-run ownership with the C11-294 native harness. Preserve the documented native-on-main residual, use a hard guest lease, and prove dismissal.

# Review C11-282 — FAIL

Head `790c98459b836dc754176fc22260ae0f8b40e14b`. Base `3786513d84b0d82c2669b2b1b066c54f0d7ada40`.

Audit finding 9 holds. Help, skill, and API text say native capture, formatting, and allocation stay on main and are not bounded by the 1 MiB response cap or the five-second caller deadline (`CLI/c11.swift:10246-10248`, `skills/c11/SKILL.md:246`, `skills/c11/references/api.md:55-57`). `read_selection.terminal` is only an id and version. The worker waits on one five-second semaphore (`Sources/SelectionRead.swift:178-186`) and does not hold a lock across the native call, so it cannot deadlock main. Main copies at most 1 MiB and then frees; the worker trims a split UTF-8 scalar after that copy (`Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift:1278-1280`, `Sources/SelectionRead.swift:197-207`). `ghostty_surface_try_read_selection` runs on main in the same turn as the live-surface check, and only `GHOSTTY_TEXT_READ_OK` is freed, once (`SurfaceHandlers.swift:1249-1281`). The blocking `ghostty_surface_read_selection` is not used. The merge kept routing, send, and rpc enabled beside selection, and kept both doc sections.

## Blocking

1. `CLI/c11.swift:3059-3073`. Acceptance criterion 1 and the skill both run `c11 read-selection --workspace <ws> --tab <t> --json` (skill: `skills/c11/SKILL.md:246`). `--json` after the command stays in `trailing`. The guard rejects it with `read-selection: unexpected arguments: --json`, so the command exits non-zero and prints no selection JSON. `jsonOutput` is set only by a `--json` that appears before the command name (`CLI/c11.swift:1744-1747`). The live proof uses that leading form (`tests_v2/test_read_selection.py:162`), so it never runs the acceptance argv. Smallest fix: treat a trailing `--json` as the JSON switch, drop it from `trailing`, and add that argv to the existing CLI assertion.

## Non-blocking

1. `skills/c11/SKILL.md:246`. `--tab tab:2` with no `--workspace` is resolved in the caller's workspace (`CLI/c11.swift:3065-3071`), same as `read-screen`. An agent in another workspace following the example reads the wrong tab, or gets not-found, instead of the operator's highlight. Show `--workspace` and `--tab` together in that example.

Not the fail reason. C11-282 is outside the risk list, and the validation comment's numbered scenario is enough for the later validator batch. The off-main wait is `min(2.0, remaining)` (`:1370`) through `waitForTerminalSurfaceOffMain` (`TerminalController.swift:3723`). Its return is discarded; the surface pointer is read only on the later main hop.

Screen lock acquisition stays `ghostty_surface_try_read_text`. BUSY fails with no allocation (`TerminalController.swift:3814-3820`). Those locks cover state only (`SelectionRead.swift:18-19`, `TerminalController.swift:22-24`) and are not held across the native call. The two handlers do not call each other. Both native reads run on main, so one turn's try-lock and free finish before the other turn's try-lock starts. A contended renderer returns BUSY to the later call. Neither path keeps a surface pointer onto the worker.

C11-258.title: launch-agent: deliver long prompts by file reference and report startup truthfully

data.from: Found during the C11-257 run (2026-10-01). Two c11 launch-agent calls (claude-code and codex) with ~1.1-1.3 KB --prompt values returned success JSON with a tab ref, but the agent never started: the rendered command was typed into the new tab's shell and cut off near 1 KB (the tty canonical-mode line limit, MAX_CANON 1024 on macOS), leaving zsh at a quote> continuation with an unterminated quote. A ~500-byte prompt in the same session worked. Observed: tab shows the truncated command ending mid-word, ps shows no agent process, the agent never registers anything. Expected: any prompt length works (deliver long prompts via a temp file or the agent's stdin rather than typing them inline), and launch-agent reports failure when the agent process does not start. Workaround: keep --prompt short and point it at a file ('Read <path> and follow it').
data.to:
## Why
A successful launch response must not strand an unattended worker at a shell continuation prompt for forty minutes. Backlog item: C8.

## Evidence
- Existing C11-258 reports two 1.1–1.3 KB --prompt launches (Claude Code and Codex) stopping at quote> while a roughly 500-byte prompt worked, with no agent process. Preserve this incident; the ticket’s MAX_CANON attribution is a hypothesis to distinguish from quoting/paste corruption.
- BACKLOG C8 records a 2026-10-01 --prompt-file launch in tab:113 stuck at > for forty minutes.
- c11 on origin/main (`0ff8887e5e`): `CLI/c11.swift:2394-2406` reads --prompt-file into a string; `Sources/DefaultAgentResolver.swift:685-699` embeds positional/flag prompts in a shell line; `Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:1389` sends that line and `:1401-1411` uses a fixed delay for post-boot prompts; `:1424-1443` returns success refs without proving process startup.
- Upstream: cmux #9875, Ghostty `f27772d10`, serializes bracketed paste as one IO message. This is a related corruption mechanism, not proof that it caused tab:113.
- Research: report 05 “The gap: top ten” #4; report 06 §1d delivery/submission distinctions; BACKLOG C8. Update C11-258 rather than create a duplicate.

## Scope
In: reproduce the launch stall, distinguish shell quoting/line limits from bracketed-paste interleaving, deliver long initial prompts through a file reference, and make launch status truthful for the tested failure paths.
Out: Ghostty atomic-paste patch (H-A), general send contract (C3), cold PTY lifecycle repairs (H-B), remote launch/holder work, new agent adapters and a universal readiness detector.

## Approach
Keep the shell launch line short; stage a private file inside c11-owned runtime storage and use the supported file-reference path or a brief that tells the agent to read it. Preserve the original prompt content without shell interpolation. Explicitly define file lifetime/cleanup so a delayed startup still reads it. Reuse the launch composer for --prompt and --prompt-file, including any saved-config path sharing it. Bound startup evidence collection off main; distinguish launch accepted/pending from observed started and surface a bounded failure for the continuation-prompt reproducer. Do not call a returned tab ref startup proof.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A reproducer with 500-byte, 1.3 KB and a substantially longer (for example 32 KiB) prompt reaches the intended agent through both --prompt and --prompt-file, without > / quote> or a truncated brief. Verify the expected full content, not just the launch exit code.
2. Fixtures containing quotes, backticks, dollar substitutions, Unicode, newlines and a prompt-file path with spaces preserve literal content and execute no injected shell command.
3. A delayed startup can still read its file; missing/unreadable files give a clear failure, and cleanup follows the documented lifetime without deleting caller-owned files.
4. The two C11-258 harnesses and the tab:113 workflow show observed process/readiness evidence. An intentionally failing executable or continuation-prompt simulation is reported as failed/pending rather than started, within a documented bound.
5. The report distinguishes a proven launch-line cause from any independently observed H-A paste corruption. Startup checks do not activate the app or alter the operator’s workspace selection.

## Validation
Use an executable launcher/PTY harness that captures literal prompt bytes and startup result, then tests_v2 and a real tagged-artifact launch using the incident providers. A computer-use pass records the launched tab and absence of continuation prompts, plus process/runtime evidence. No full soak is required unless the implementation adds ongoing hot-path work; a bounded repeated-launch check belongs on Atlas. Preserve existing C11-258 history.

Builds and soaks run on Atlas once F1 / C11-216 lands, through the build lock. Use a tagged artifact and its socket, launched with C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh (or the tagged automation launcher); never an untagged DEV app. Record exact artifact/head and distinguish fixture assertions from the real product pass. Update affected CLI/event skill contracts, run scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh for edited installable skills and verify the installed copy.

## Dependencies
Existing ticket: C11-258, update in place. Related C11-257 supplied the reproducer. H-A owns upstream #9875; add a hard dependency only if reproduction proves its fix is required, and report that to the lead through the ticket. C3 owns send delivery vocabulary; F1 / C11-216 supplies tagged build capacity.

## Risks
Quoting, TTY limits and paste framing can produce similar symptoms; prove the cause before choosing the patch. Private temporary prompts must not leak through public fixtures, command logs or launcher JSON. Keep telemetry parsing, I/O, deduplication and sorting off main; apply only the minimal UI mutation asynchronously. Preserve the hitTest pointer guard, TabItemView equality boundary and allocation-free forceRefresh path. No tenant config writes or trust broadening. Localize new product strings in English plus ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; validate interpolation tokens. Sanitize fixtures, screenshots and logs before inclusion in this public repository.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional per-process observation and explicit operator actions only; no blocking bridge, automatic approval or persistent tenant configuration.

# C11-258 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL**

PR #512. Reviewed head `0541d26b1d1505afc736d25028008c22e8b0caf2` against merge-base `86d45e218f220c89b592653de2f1c488d57068f7`. Re-fetched origin/main and the PR branch and confirmed the PR still names this head before posting. One static pass covered all 25 changed files and the shared launch, input-queue, configuration and tab-lifetime seams. No builds, tests or product launches were performed by this reviewer.

## Blocking

1. **Post-boot launch text merges into the shell command if terminal attachment takes longer than 2.5 seconds.** `Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:1421` changes the initial launcher to `sendSubmitFormText(plan.launchLine)`, while `:1438-1442` starts the post-boot timer immediately and submits the file instruction without checking whether the first submission reached the terminal. Kimi and GitHub Copilot use this delivery shape (`Sources/AgentManifest.swift:444,492`). For a terminal whose surface remains nil through that timer, both calls take the unchanged helper's queue path (`Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:4047-4057`): they append text without a separator, set the same Boolean submit flag, and finish their transactions. On attachment, `:4408-4426` writes both chunks and sends only one Return. With the factory Kimi command the shell receives `kimi --autoRead the file at ... and follow it exactly.` instead of a launcher followed by a TUI prompt. The agent cannot ingest the intended brief. This applies to short prompts too.

   This is the plan's explicit delayed-attachment case and the brief's requirement to support post-boot kinds, not a request to repair the general cold-terminal lifecycle. The new launch call site removes the previous launch-line newline but uses a helper that does not preserve multiple queued submit boundaries. `c11Tests/LaunchPromptDeliveryTests.swift:81-89` checks composition only; its executable PTY test covers positional/flag delivery into an already-ready shell, so neither catches this integration failure.

   **Smallest fix:** sequence post-boot delivery locally to launch so its delay begins after the launcher has actually been submitted; do not enqueue both submissions into an unattached terminal's single-submit buffer. Preserve the existing best-effort TUI delay and keep C11-257's send/mailbox implementation untouched. Add an Atlas behavioral case that holds attachment beyond 2.5 seconds, attaches, and observes a separate launcher execution and exact file-read receipt. This finding is source-traced; the reproducer has not been executed by this reviewer.

## Non-blocking

None requiring changes. The private store preserves UTF-8 bytes, uses exclusive 0600 files in 0700 namespaces, binds cleanup to the terminal object, and documents crash leftovers. Startup evidence is explicitly process-only and conservatively remains pending when identity is unproven. No send/mailbox implementation or installed skill was changed by this diff.

## Runtime proof still required

- Owner artifact `art_01M3XKPWR9EHKGYEQ10NNKYYT7` records exact-head Atlas targeted tests and build, synthetic packaged-app file reads, and native Claude/Codex foreground startup. Those are owner-provided results, not an independent rerun. Both native receipt fields are false, so native ingestion is still unproved. The proposed Validator byte-count/SHA256 receipts would establish ingestion for the specified Claude/Codex matrix once actually observed; merely repeating startup=started would not.
- Extend the batch scenario to the post-boot Kimi/Copilot delivery path, including the delayed-attachment reproducer above, plus the flag-delivery path. The attached smoke script `art_01M3XKPWTRM2MP82XEA05W4D9Q` exercises only Claude/Codex argv templates. The current scenario's statement that post-boot remains best effort does not exercise its bytes or submission boundaries. This coverage gap is part of blocking finding 1.
- On the corrected tagged Atlas artifact, complete the proposed 500 B / 1.3 KB / 32 KiB inline/file and saved-config matrix, Settings/New Workspace/existing-tab paths, delayed read and close cleanup, caller-file preservation, failure/pending deadline cases, and selected-workspace/macOS-focus checks. Keep process startup, ingestion receipts and visible-state evidence separate. Native ingestion remains a batch Validator obligation under the review brief; its deferral alone is not an additional code finding.

data.from:
## Why
An operator or orchestrator needs to collect a run's workspaces into named folders and rearrange the fleet in one predictable operation. Backlog item: W1.

## Evidence
- c11: `Sources/Workspace.swift:245-262` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) snapshots color, pin state and metadata; `Sources/SessionPersistence.swift:490-522` has workspace and manager snapshots without groups.
- c11: `Sources/WorkspaceManager.swift:2354-2409` has pin-aware individual moves; `Sources/SocketHandlers/WorkspaceHandlers.swift:27-28` routes the singular reorder. `Sources/WorkspaceManager.swift:5687-5703` restores workspace UUIDs.
- Upstream: cmux #4815/#5018 groups and CLI, #4507 batch reorder. At upstream/main (920ff39ff7), inspect `Packages/macOS/CmuxWorkspaces/Sources/CmuxWorkspaces/Values/WorkspaceGroup.swift`, `Reorder/WorkspaceReorderPlanner.swift` under that package, and `Packages/macOS/CmuxControlSocket/Sources/CmuxControlSocket/Coordinator/WorkspaceGroup/`. Its anchor-workspace machinery is reference material, not c11's model.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md`, What cmux built §1h/§3 and proposal §3; `feature-audit-astra.md` Grab list rows 4.8/4.12/4.12b; `feature-audit-fable.md` row 4.12. BACKLOG.md D17/W1 supersedes the older timing recommendation in `c11-1.0.html` §4 and folds batch reorder 4.8 into this item. Auto-filing by root remains cut.

## Scope
In: folder model `WorkspaceGroup {id, name, color, icon, isCollapsed, isPinned}`, `Workspace.groupId`, group/member ordering, backward-compatible session persistence, CLI/socket verbs, tree projection and skill documentation. CLI: `c11 workspace-group list|create|rename|delete|ungroup|add|remove|move|collapse|expand|pin|unpin|set-color|set-icon|focus`, all with `--json`; `reorder-workspaces --order --dry-run` and actual apply.
Out: W2 sidebar, W3 integrated validation, W4 history; anchor workspaces, automatic membership by root, automatic naming, stable short numbers across restart (D15), sidebar/AppKit rewrite, remote federation and account restore. Group removal does not implicitly close member workspaces.

## Approach
Use a folder record owned alongside the workspace collection, with member order derived from that collection. Reuse c11's color/icon and UUID-resolution seams. Specify group pin/member pin precedence and window scope before implementation; do not inherit anchor promotion or generate hidden terminals. Decode older snapshots as ungrouped. Factor a pure reorder plan that validates the whole request, then apply one model mutation; dry-run uses exactly the same planner. Preserve selected workspace and tab for non-focus verbs; only group focus may select, without activating or raising the app. Update `skills/c11/SKILL.md` and the applicable API reference, sync the installed skill, and verify its live contents.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A tagged-build CLI scenario creates an empty folder, adds two existing workspaces, exercises every listed verb and reads equivalent identities, member order and properties through list/tree JSON. Removing the final member leaves a valid empty folder; no generated workspace or PTY appears.
2. Delete/ungroup fixtures preserve member workspaces, their terminal processes and selection. Duplicate membership, unknown group/workspace and wrong-window targets return specific errors without a partial mutation.
3. A mixed pinned/unpinned fixture tests individual and batch moves. Dry-run changes no order or focus; applying it from unchanged input yields the reported order, preserving the documented pinned segments and unaffected member order. Duplicate/unknown batch IDs leave the complete original order intact. Emit `workspace.reordered` only on a real apply change.
4. Save/restart/restore preserves group UUIDs, membership, order, name, color, icon, collapse and pin state. A pre-group snapshot restores ungrouped; an orphaned membership fixture has a documented recovery without losing its workspace.
5. Run the non-focus verbs with another workspace selected and with c11 backgrounded: selection and macOS focus stay unchanged. Explicit group focus selects its documented live member or reports an empty group without manufacturing one.
6. Bundled and installed skill examples accurately exercise the shipped CLI and JSON shape; no persistent tab/group ordinal guarantee is introduced.

## Validation
Behavioral tests for the group/reorder planner and old/new snapshot fixtures; tests_v2 CLI/socket scenarios against a tagged socket; tagged-app inspection of unchanged terminals/selection and one restore. W2/W3 own full sidebar computer-use coverage. Measure reorder/group churn under typing against F2's preregistered baseline. Builds and soaks run on Atlas after F1/C11-216, through build-lock entry points; launch tagged QA builds only. No source-text assertion tests.

## Dependencies
F1 (C11-216) for build/soak execution; F2 for comparative performance evidence. Batch reorder 4.8 is included here, not a separate ticket. W2 consumes this model and API; W3 validates the integrated result. Cross-workstream links are for the lead.

## Risks
Extra collection publications can affect typing latency; keep disk I/O/planning off typing paths and minimize main-thread mutation. Snapshot migration and pin normalization must not drop workspaces. No tenant configuration writes. Localize any new user-facing strings in English plus ja/uk/ko/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ru, preserving format tokens. Public tickets, fixtures and captures must use synthetic paths/names and contain no private fleet/session data.

Size: L. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: explicit operator/agent-composed folders, with no inference about agent work or tenant configuration changes.
