C11-276.title: Emit advisory Codex and Grok turn edges from transcript observation

data.from:
## Why
An agent with no trusted hook should not appear working for its entire TUI lifetime when its transcript contains a supported turn boundary. Missing transcript evidence must remain visible. Backlog item: J5.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Sources/AgentModelDetection.swift:88` has only prompt/agent/tool-result events; `:399` maps Codex task_started and `:400` maps task_complete as generic output. `:167` reads Grok summary.json rather than turn edges; `:641` shows only model/last_active_at. `:273` skips to the final 4 MiB on a large backlog.
- Upstream: report 01 identifies open classifier PR #15276 as research, not shipped hookless parity. No upstream producer is assumed reusable.
- Research: BACKLOG.md J5/D4; report 01 Transcript reading; Fable J5; Astra §4 transcript counterexample and §6 D4.

## Scope
In: reuse the AgentModelDetection observation lane for Codex/Grok turn.started, turn.completed and turn.interrupted at transcript confidence; gap/freshness reporting and hook dedupe. Out: blocked-state inference, screen classifiers, Kimi/Copilot/Gemini parity, changing provider files, or treating Grok last_active_at as a completed turn.

## Approach
Extend the incremental parser only from versioned F3 evidence. Locate a real Grok turn/event source rather than invent edges from summary timestamps; if a version lacks an edge, report that capability as unavailable. Preserve bounded reads, partial-line buffering, rotation/truncation and per-conversation reset. Send structural events to J2 with stable identities/source rank; skip gaps degrade coverage rather than creating imagined transitions. Source confidence and evidence age must reach consumers.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Supported Codex and Grok start/completion/interruption records in F3 emit their semantic edge exactly once on repeated polls. Absent native edge types are declared unavailable, with no fabricated completion or interrupt.
2. The Esc incident uses a recorded interrupt marker where available; an assistant/tool output record alone does not claim completion and a quiet transcript never claims blocked.
3. A poll backlog larger than 4 MiB reports a coverage gap/degraded freshness. Partial final lines, truncate/replace and session change do not replay old-session edges into the new tab lifecycle.
4. Where a hook and transcript report the same turn, J2’s source/confidence policy avoids duplicate turns and a lower-confidence late observation does not overturn the fixture’s newer authoritative state.
5. The roster/consumer data exposes transcript provenance and advisory status; polling remains bounded/off-main and no transcript bodies survive into the durable journal or diagnostics.

## Validation
Use executable parser/tailer fixtures with temp files for append, split line, rotation, >4 MiB gaps and session changes; replay through J2. Compare actual Codex/Grok UI turn completion and interruption on an Atlas-built tagged app, using a verified display, timer and dismissal. Measure the existing polling lane under F2’s fleet workload on Atlas.

## Dependencies
Depends on J2; F3 is the captured oracle. J4 hooks are optional stronger evidence, not a prerequisite. Coordinate provenance/freshness fields with J6 and interval gaps with J7; J8 documents the limits.

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.

C11-274.title: Widen Claude lifecycle observations through per-process hooks

data.from:
## Why
Claude’s bypass-mode question/plan prompts and error stops must produce the correct reason instead of relying on a notification that may never arrive. Backlog item: J3.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `Resources/bin/claude:207` supplies six hooks, including async PreToolUse, through the temp settings file at `:226`; `CLI/c11.swift:17006` caches a question and `:17036` relies on Notification rather than a blocked event.
- Upstream: #15232 StopFailure; #15666/#15887 child/background-work handling; #6606 bypass questions. `CLI/CMUXCLI+ClaudeHookSettings.swift:16` includes StopFailure and `:85` shows the blocking PermissionRequest bridge that c11 must not import.
- Research: BACKLOG.md J3; report 01 producer table; report 03 The gap; Fable event-journal table and Astra §5 observation-before-storage.

## Scope
In: StopFailure, observe-only PermissionRequest, async PostToolUse, SubagentStart/Stop, PreCompact, and bypass AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode mapping through the existing per-process --settings file. Out: blocking PermissionRequest bridge, answers/tool bodies in storage, automatic menu typing, other providers, C11-257 message delivery and duplicating A1 fixes.

## Approach
Extend the existing hook settings and CLI mapper into J2 append. Extract only event kind, structural reason, IDs and timing; the PermissionRequest observer must return promptly without emitting a decision. Preserve async PreToolUse, add async PostToolUse, scope child events to the child, and preserve operator settings merge and wrapper pass-through. Reuse any A1 bypass/scoped-clear repair already landed; one owner for the blocked reason.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Replay and observe F3 normal versus bypass Claude captures: PreToolUse AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode open the appropriate blocked reasons even without PermissionRequest/Notification; Stop is a completion rather than a blocked ask.
2. StopFailure produces error evidence; child spawn/stop records do not finish or unblock the root. PreCompact is a bounded observation with the reviewed mapping, not a fabricated completion.
3. The late async PreToolUse/PostToolUse fixture after Stop leaves the completed result intact; a tool beginning in tab B does not clear tab A’s wait.
4. The normal-mode PermissionRequest observer neither answers nor waits for an operator response through c11. New hooks remain bounded when the socket is unavailable, and Claude continues through its own native permission flow.
5. Wrapper behavioral checks preserve operator settings and outside-c11 pass-through, and the resulting journal/spool contains no prompt/tool bodies or answer content.

## Validation
Use F3 mapper/replay tests plus executable wrapper tests with a controlled fake CLI and temp settings; then observe real Claude normal/bypass flows on an Atlas-built tagged app/socket. Record supported Claude versions. Run the registered lifecycle-burst soak on Atlas; UI proof requires actual prompt/mark observation, a verified display, timer and dismissal.

## Dependencies
Depends on J2. Coordinate A1 (bypass question and sibling clears) without filing duplicate work. J8 documents D5 and adapter coverage; C11-257 remains a separate message-delivery scope.

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.

C11-274 validation. Head 5393670a60b4d6580252fbcbc7e8d555092a1475. The Atlas run covered this tree before the commit; the commit is that tree.

Evidence
1. Atlas remote-build tag c11-274-claude-hooks, mode test, only c11LogicTests/ClaudeHookMappingTests. Invocation 37e6f95ce2a24d258872c80ce4699bf4. Result: 5 tests, 0 failures, TEST SUCCEEDED. Cases: bypass ask stays blocked until matching resume, stop-failure/child/pre-compact, late and sibling tool, permission request drops bodies, shared fixture corpus.
2. Wrapper script on the build host: PASS. Twelve hook keys. PermissionRequest timeout 1, not async, command c11 claude-hook permission-request. PostToolUse matcher empty, async, timeout 5. Missing, stale, and outside-c11 sockets pass argv through. Unwritable TMPDIR falls back to inline JSON. A temp HOME gained no .claude/settings.json.
3. Built CLI on the build host: permission-request stdout is {}, exit 0, under 0.75s. Unreachable socket spooled one structural approval.requested draft for Bash, request_id tool-1, tool_class other, reason_code null, no sentinel bodies, no decision keys. AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode permission-request appended nothing and still printed {}. A live fake socket appended one approval.requested row and no clear_notifications, set_status, or report_agent_activity.
4. Built CLI resolution check: AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode PostToolUse still append attention.resolved resumed and still clear notifications and set Running. Ordinary Bash PostToolUse appends state.changed tool_activity and does not clear notifications, set status, or call report_agent_activity.

StopFailure fold gap
StopFailure emits agent.error.reported, native_event other, reason_code null, is_child false. The landed reducer returns observation for an unknown native name before the kind switch, so the parent phase stays unchanged. C11-272 says unknown native events have no parent lifecycle effect. The journal row is error evidence. It does not move the parent to phase error. This ticket does not change JournalReducer.

Repeated matching resolution after completion does not reopen working. The landed fold returns resolution_not_correlated once the phase is no longer blocked. Covered by ClaudeHookMappingTests.

No operator_response. UserPromptSubmit stays turn.started and does not copy a prior request id. PostToolUse and UserPromptSubmit get distinct event ids. A retained draft is byte-identical on retry. Child spawn and stop do not finish the parent. PreCompact is observation and does not change phase. Missing agent_id stays unattributed with is_child true.

Validator scenario
1. Launch the tagged build from this head. Open one Claude tab in normal permission mode.
2. Cause AskUserQuestion with no Notification. The tab stays waiting. A Stop while that ask is unresolved stays blocked.
3. Continue past the same tool_use_id. The journal row is attention.resolved with resolution resumed, then Stop leaves the tab idle completed.
4. Cause a Bash PermissionRequest. Claude's own permission UI still appears. The journal row is approval.requested. c11 does not allow or deny. Hook stdout is {}.
5. After Stop, deliver a late PreToolUse for that same turn. The tab stays idle completed.
6. Spawn a subagent and let it finish. The parent tab does not go idle because of the child.
7. Read the journal rows and confirm they contain no question text, tool_input, tool_response, last_assistant_message, or custom_instructions.

# C11-274 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL** at `a80794899f5293dac2dc271814b9fecb32062d66`.

Base: `9f2173320a9dac428edaef1512dc0271b766802a` (fresh merge-base with origin/main). Reviewed all nine PR files and their delivery, attribution, reducer, and fixture seams. Also reviewed the delta from `5393670a60b4d6580252fbcbc7e8d555092a1475`: the merge brings in C11-314's three test-file changes; the hook implementation and its tests are unchanged. The detached checkout is clean. No builds or tests were run by this reviewer. The owner's Atlas results are reported evidence for the earlier tree, not independently executed runtime proof. Current-head build, compatibility, and mailbox CI were still running at the final check.

## Blocking

1. **P1 — Making the existing ask-resolution hook asynchronous loses completion ordering.** `Resources/bin/claude:241`; `Sources/Journal/ClaudeHookMapping.swift:30`; unchanged `Sources/Journal/JournalReducer.swift:125` and `:141`. Concrete AC1/AC3 sequence: PreToolUse opens question/plan request A; the operator answers; Claude schedules the now-async PostToolUse(A), completes the turn, and its synchronous Stop reaches c11 first. Stop is discarded as `unresolved_request`, preserving blocked and no terminal barrier. The delayed matching resolution then changes blocked to working. With no further Stop, the finished turn stays working. This is the answer/continuation fixture with the same delayed-hook delivery condition already named in AC3, not a hypothetical crash. The tests only delay ordinary Bash activity and repeat resolution after an already-applied completion; neither exercises this order. **Smallest fix:** preserve C11-273's ordered callback for AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode while broadening ordinary PostToolUse asynchronously, with a strictly bounded delivery path. If all PostToolUse callbacks must be async, resolve that dependency/contract conflict with the journal owner before landing; do not silently weaken the completion oracle or add a second fold. Add the answer → Stop-before-resolution regression for both blocking tools.

2. **P1 — The new synchronous observer can block before the bounded append and lose its draft.** `CLI/c11.swift:17649` and `:18115`, through `:2130`, `:2160`, `:5264`, and `:615`. The initial 250 ms deadline is restored immediately after connect. Authentication then uses the ordinary socket timeout (10 seconds by default), and the new `appendResolvedJournal()` performs session-store lookup under blocking `flock(LOCK_EX)` before reaching `JournalCommand.deliver`'s separate 250 ms budget. A connected peer that withholds its auth reply, or a held hook-state lock during lifecycle traffic, therefore holds PermissionRequest beyond the plan's 250 ms budget. Claude's one-second hook timeout can kill it before `{}` or a spool write; auth errors also escape before the advisory dispatch catch. StopFailure can wait longer under its ten-second wrapper timeout. The added test uses an absent socket and permits 0.75 seconds (`tests/test_claude_hook_permission_cli.py:77`); its live peer answers immediately. **Smallest fix:** cover authentication, owner lookup, and append with one bounded observer path; on timeout/lock contention retain the pre-created structural draft through the existing spool and return the neutral output. Avoid the blocking session-store operation on this observer path or give it bounded acquisition. Atlas must exercise a connected-but-silent authenticated peer and held state lock, not only ENOENT.

3. **P1 — StopFailure does not meet the plan's error-state oracle; the test substitutes the opposite result.** `Sources/Journal/ClaudeHookMapping.swift:41`; `c11Tests/ClaudeHookMappingTests.swift:73`. A working root receiving StopFailure produces `errorReported` with `nativeEvent=other` and null reason. The landed reducer returns observation at `Sources/Journal/JournalReducer.swift:23`; even an allowlisted native name would need `reasonCode=sessionFailure` at `:167` to enter error. The new test explicitly requires the root to remain working. The owner's validation comment candidly records this gap, but plan AC2 explicitly requires “StopFailure fold → error.” The plan's mapping table and C11-272 unknown-native rule conflict with that oracle. **Smallest fix:** obtain an explicit Orchestrator resolution of that contract conflict, then align mapping and behavioral test with the agreed oracle. If error projection remains required, coordinate the narrow schema/mapping dependency rather than disguising StopFailure as Stop or weakening the test. Logging an error-kind row alone does not satisfy the current phase-error acceptance.

4. **P2 — Fixture replay and the deferred Validator script leave required incidents unproved.** `c11Tests/ClaudeHookMappingTests.swift:163`, especially `:170–186`, and validation comment `ev_01M3YJN7YXJCKY83MHMH1H70MS`, “Validator scenario.” The replay selects three files, drops their oracle records and tab attribution, and checks only a hard-coded final phase. It does not replay the captured normal-tool or sibling-while-waiting cases against their intended checkpoints. Its answered case is explicitly a synthetic extension. The seven-step runtime script launches only normal mode and omits bypass AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, PreCompact, a StopFailure probe/version-supported gap, the two-live-tab sibling case, and late PostToolUse. Consequently the allowed later batch cannot establish the omitted AC1–3 claims. **Smallest fix:** use the shared corpus's relevant owner identities and per-step intended oracles, retaining observed/derived/synthetic/gap labels, and add those missing numbered Validator cases with provider version and the required lifecycle-burst check. Include a real native answer/continuation correlation capture. Deferred execution itself is allowed; an inadequate deferred scenario is the blocker.

## Non-blocking

None. The mapper is structurally allowlisted: it copies no prompt, tool body, answer, error text, custom instructions, or path. Child identifiers remain separate from the parent session, absent child identity remains absent, ordinary PostToolUse cannot resolve attention, and UserPromptSubmit does not fabricate request correlation. No new tenant-config writes, transcript reads, localization surface, main-thread calls, or notification-clearing calls were introduced. The wrapper retains per-process tempfile settings and pass-through/fallback behavior. App/CLI mapper membership and logic-test membership are present.

## Acceptance evidence

| Row | Reviewed evidence and remaining limit |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Mapper+fold tests cover both blocking tools, absent/mismatched request IDs, unresolved Stop, ordered resume/completion, and repeated resolution. Finding 1 breaks the newly asynchronous production order; finding 4 leaves native normal/bypass correlation incomplete. |
| AC2 | Child and PreCompact tests exercise the reducer and preserve the root. StopFailure asserts working, contrary to the plan's error oracle (finding 3). |
| AC3 | Synthetic ordinary late-tool and sibling tests exist. Captured sibling checkpoints and required deferred live scenarios are absent; delayed ask resolution is not covered (findings 1 and 4). |
| AC4 | Executable CLI tests check neutral stdout, structural spooling for a missing socket, and a responsive fake peer. They do not establish the aggregate deadline or graceful stalled-auth/lock behavior (finding 2). Native permission UI remains batch proof. |
| AC5 | Executable wrapper tests inspect injected JSON, fallback, pass-through, and absence of tenant settings writes. Mapper/CLI sentinel tests substantiate body exclusion. Existing operator-settings merge and real journal readback still need the native batch path. The in-memory `let retry = first` equality assertion is not delivery/retry proof. |

## Runtime proof still required

On Atlas, run the corrected mapper/reducer and built-CLI tests at the final landing head, including delayed ask/plan resolution, silent authenticated socket, held state lock, and actual retry/spool identity preservation. CI must finish successfully. These establish the fixes, independently of a green result for the current five tests.

C11-274 is not on the contract's risk list, so the tagged native UI proof may run in the Validator's merged-main batch once the numbered script is complete. That script must cover normal and bypass questions/plans and their actual native resolution IDs; native Bash permission UI without a c11 answer; StopFailure or an explicit version-supported gap; child isolation; PreCompact journal readback; late Pre/PostToolUse and two-tab waiting preservation; operator settings merge; body-free journal/spool readback; and the registered lifecycle burst. Record Claude version, verified display, a hard timer, and proven dismissal. This verdict does not fail the ticket merely because that batch has not run.

## Blocking

**B1. Bounded child shutdown parks main for the HUP grace.** `src/termio/Exec.zig:226-246` (`threadExit`, stopping path) calls `stopClosingPty()` → `stopWithOptions` → `killCommandWithTimeouts` → `killProcessGroupsWithTimeouts` (`Exec.zig:~1270-1420`), which sleeps in 10 ms polls up to `sighup_grace` 12 s plus `sigkill_grace` 3 s. `threadExit` runs on the IO thread, and `Surface.deinit` joins that thread on the app thread (`src/Surface.zig:830-833`), reached from `ghostty_surface_free` on the main actor (`Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3297`, `:4513`, `:4556`).

Failure scenario: close a tab whose foreground job ignores SIGHUP (the validation's own `ignore-hup` and `ignore-both` cases: 12106 ms and 12153 ms). For those 12 s the main thread sits in `Surface.deinit` → `pthread_join`; every terminal, every socket command through `v2MainSync`, and the hang monitor's `Surface.deinit lock-wait` signature (the 08-25 incident's) all fire. Before this PR the shell-plus-ignoring-job shape closed in ~35 ms and leaked the job (B022); the direct-child-ignores shape hung forever (B062). So this is a planned ceiling that the ticket's AC6 ("returns within the deadline") and the plan ("close ceiling is the phase budget") accepted, but neither names that the ceiling is a main-thread park, and the fixture's close timings were taken after the latency sampling, so the stall is absent from the reported distributions. For a public 1.0 whose top incident class is main parks, I am not willing to pass it silently.

Smallest fix: keep `killProcessGroupsWithTimeouts` as is (tests stay synchronous), and in `stopWithOptions` when `close_pty` is true (the cancelled-teardown path only), copy the numeric ids (`pid`, primary pgid, foreground pgid, timeouts) and run the escalation/reap loop on a spawned, detached `std.Thread`, logging on error. `waitpid` on the direct child works from any thread; `ECHILD` is already handled. The IO thread then returns within one poll interval and main sees the graceful-case ~50-100 ms. If the Orchestrator rules the planned ceiling acceptable for 1.0 instead, this drops to non-blocking and the diff otherwise passes; the fallback without a thread is to cut `sighup_grace` to ~1 s and `sigkill_grace` to ~1 s, which still leaves a 2 s beachball and gives cooperative jobs less time.

## B1 verification

- **Main returns fast.** `Subprocess.stopWithOptions` (`Exec.zig:1135-1152`) on the `close_pty` path, which only `threadExit`'s cancelled-teardown branch takes, copies `cmd.pid`, clears `self.process`, and starts a `DetachedShutdown` with `{primary_pgid, foreground_pgid, direct_child_pid, timeouts}` by value; the process-null foreground-group path (`Exec.zig:1176-1186`) does the same. The IO thread returns within the PTY close plus one `tcgetpgrp`, and main's join follows. The Windows and flatpak branches, the init-error path (`stop()` without `close_pty`), and all `kill*WithTimeouts` helpers stay synchronous, so existing tests are unchanged.
- **No use-after-free.** `DetachedShutdown.run` (`Exec.zig:1263-1292`) calls `killProcessGroupsWithTimeouts` with only numeric ids and `KillTimeouts` values. That function touches `c.getpgrp()`, `killpg`, `sysctl` (`processIgnoresSignal`), `waitpid` (`reapExitedChild`) and the scoped logger; nothing dereferences `Subprocess`, `Command`, `Pty`, `ThreadData` or the `Surface`. `self.process = null` is set before the spawn, so `Subprocess.deinit`'s later `stop()` (idempotent via `stopped`) and the PTY release cannot race the reaper on shared storage. Spawn failure falls back to the synchronous bounded loop with a logged diagnostic rather than abandoning the waitable child, which is the right failure direction.
- **Reaping still happens.** `reapExitedChild` already handles `ECHILD` for a watcher-won race; the IO loop is stopped before `threadExit`, so the xev process watcher cannot consume the status after the handoff. The new test `cancelled subprocess close returns before grace and detached worker reaps` (`Exec.zig:1881-1927`) asserts return under 250 ms with `stopped`/`process`/`pty` cleared, then sets the owners to `undefined` and waits for `kill(pid, 0)` → `ESRCH` without calling `waitpid` itself, then `expectReaped` (`ECHILD`). That is the right oracle for both prompt return and reaper-owned reaping. Both builds used an actual default zsh terminal with unchanged injected fields. `CMUX_TAB_ID` and `CMUX_PANEL_ID` held the owned **tab** UUID. `CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID` held a distinct owned **workspace** UUID.

After an external checkout and one foreground Git commit, disk HEAD was `fixture-next`, the same attributed HEAD watcher remained alive, and the automatically emitted payload was:

```text
report_git_branch fixture-next --tab=<owned-tab> --panel=<owned-tab>
```

The earlier payload contained an additional empty dirty-option space, with the same routing values. The candidate payload omitted dirty status. A process-scoped observational wrapper retained and forwarded the original `_cmux_send` payload unchanged. No environment routing field was patched. The sidebar stayed `fixture-main clean` for eight seconds on both builds. Candidate trace clock was unavailable; its original order is retained. Earlier-build trace includes epoch timestamps.

A **separate manual control** sent:

```text
report_git_branch fixture-next --tab=<owned-workspace> --panel=<owned-tab>
```

Both servers acknowledged `OK`, and their sidebar immediately became `fixture-next clean`. Both commits exited 0 with no `index.lock` error. This control isolates the routing seam; it is not automatic-path PASS evidence.

Source corroborates the runtime: `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3536` injects the tab UUID into CMUX_TAB_ID; `Resources/shell-integration/cmux-zsh-integration.zsh:253` forwards that value in --tab; `Sources/TerminalController.swift:670` parses --tab as workspace; `Sources/SocketHandlers/SocketDispatch.swift:489` looks up that workspace and silently returns when it does not exist. The shell-activity handler already resolves workspace from panel, but the Git handler does not. The injected-tab value dates to commit `bcebbbc2035`; the routing-handler assumption exists in the approved earlier build. Candidate/earlier execution, not source inspection alone, establishes the pre-existing classification.

The owner's JSON sidebar oracle was also corrected in the ignored runtime driver: v2 sidebar.state emits counts and agent chip, not Git branch; the ordinary text sidebar-state response exposes the actual branch state. This fixture correction did not change the observed automatic failure.

## Scoped passing evidence

The exact shipped-shell fixture passed all 11 executable cases on the build host in 41.301 seconds, including synthetic reused-PID/start-time identity, actual parent SIGKILL, blocked descendant teardown, timeout and recovery. Its app executable matched the canonical build-host manifest SHA256 `4f964b60873ddb4dfae4153ea2e1308605ba0995480acb344e2614e3fc6524ac` before and after execution.

Every case captured PID plus start-time identity. Blocked probes owned a ready TERM-ignoring child before the parent was terminated. All recorded watcher/probe/child generations disappeared within three seconds. Bash is an explicitly started matching PTY sourced from the shipped bash integration; only zsh is claimed as default startup wiring. The standalone normal-exit case captures the new preexec HEAD watcher generation before exit.

An ordinary zsh login shell and a clean bash shell outside the app had no c11 watcher function, tab ID or socket environment. Tenant file hash comparisons remained unchanged. Synthetic fixture Git identity and fake gh were local to disposable repositories and their shell PATH. No real GitHub request, account installation or auth mutation occurred.

## Separate App-menu Quit gate

A background own-PID accessibility menu-click did not terminate the owned guest app within the separate 20-second deadline. The shell and PR watcher therefore still had a live parent. This is retained as an automation/quit gate, with no orphan-cleanup PASS or C11-305 regression claim. Attributed cleanup subsequently proved the owned app PID absent. C11-287.title: Replace a crashed web view on the next turn and stop forced layout

data.from:
## Why
A WebContent crash that runs inside WebKit's callback, or a forced layout from that path, takes down the process. Every terminal in the app goes with it. cmux saw that crash about 1,900 times in one release on macOS 26. Backlog item: B1.

## Evidence
- c11: `Sources/Tabs/BrowserTab.swift:6451-6455` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e). `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` calls `didTerminateWebContentProcess`. The navigation delegate sets that to `replaceWebViewAfterContentProcessTermination` at `:2935-2936`.
- c11: `replaceWebViewAfterContentProcessTermination` (`:3515-3520`) calls `replaceWebViewPreservingState` (`:3523-3603`) immediately. That builds a new `WKWebView` (`:3562-3568`), detaches the portal, and restores the URL on the same stack as the callback. There is no deferral to the next turn.
- c11: forced synchronous layout is still in the portal refresh. `Sources/BrowserWindowPortal.swift:3300-3312` calls `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded` and `displayIfNeeded`, including `(webView.window ?? hostView.window)?.displayIfNeeded()`. `Sources/Tabs/BrowserTabView.swift:6171-6173` does the same on the web view, the slot, and the host.
- Upstream: cmux #9773 and #9774 (forced layout) and #12519 (in-callback swap). #4987 is the older process-pool plus recovery PR. The pool half is not the fix. Report 06 says `WKProcessPool` is believed deprecated for process assignment. Do not verify that by shipping a pool.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §5 "Process isolation", and `05-bug-sweep.md` top-10 item 10 and ranked rows 10 and 11. Astra row 4.18: recovery already exists. Harden it. Do not port a second stack. `c11-1.0.html` marks it core. Bug track H-E is browser automation correctness (cookies, state load, fill, eval, screenshots). It is a neighbor in `BrowserTab.swift`, not this fix.

## Scope
In: the termination callback returns without creating a web view. The replacement runs on a later main-queue turn, still on the main actor, and only if that web view is still current. Loading and focus state reset as the existing `replaceWebViewPreservingState` already does. Remove the forced `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded` and `displayIfNeeded` from the portal refresh path that runs during SwiftUI updates (`BrowserWindowPortal.swift:3300-3312` and the matching block in `BrowserTabView.swift:6171-6173`). A second crash while a replacement is pending does not start a second replacement.
Out: a new `WKProcessPool` per tab. Passkeys. The URL allowlist. H-E automation bugs (whole-profile cookie clear, `state load` into the old document, React fill, CSP eval, stale screenshots). Popup management as a new subsystem. If this tab already tracks child popups, close those that belong to the terminated view. Do not build a popup manager to find them. C11-197, C11-202, and C11-205 (main-thread hangs elsewhere).

## Approach
Set a flag in `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` and `DispatchQueue.main.async` the existing replace function. Guard on `isCurrentWebView` the way `:3491` already does. Keep `debugSimulateWebContentProcessTermination` (`:3607`) as the test hook, and point it at the deferred path so tests do not bypass the fix. For the layout sites, delete the synchronous layout and display calls that exist only to flush a portal update. Leave ordinary AppKit layout alone. If a page stays blank without one of those calls, restore a single layout on the next run-loop turn and record why, rather than putting `displayIfNeeded` back inside the SwiftUI update. Coordinate with whoever picks up H-E so two PRs do not rewrite `replaceWebViewPreservingState` at once.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `debugSimulateWebContentProcessTermination` on a tagged build reloads the same URL, and the terminal tabs in that window still accept input afterwards. The ghostty log shows no crash.
2. A unit or harness test observes that `webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` returns before `makeWebView` runs. The replacement happens on a later turn. A second terminate before that turn produces one replacement, not two.
3. The portal refresh path no longer calls `displayIfNeeded` on the window. A browser tab beside a terminal still paints after a split resize and after the simulated crash. Check both with a screenshot or computer use.
4. A page that crashes twice in a row ends on the existing error or restored URL, not in a loop that pins a core. Cap or coalesce. Document the cap in the PR.
5. An H-E behavior this PR does not claim to change still works: `c11 browser snapshot` on a live page returns a tree. One check is enough.

## Validation
A harness test for the deferral (criterion 2) that does not need a host app if the callback can be invoked on a test double. Otherwise `c11-unit` is host-bound. Run that only with a granted slot, or leave it for CI. Computer-use pass on a tagged build for criteria 1, 3, and 5. No soak. This path is not the keystroke path. Do not add an app-level display link or a `ghostty_surface_draw` loop.

## Dependencies
Bug track H-E is not ticketed from this workstream. Name it in the PR and do not absorb it. No backlog id inside cli-browser-release blocks this. X1 translates any new visible string, such as a crashed-page line if one is added. Prefer the existing error page over a new string.

## Risks
Typing latency: `displayIfNeeded` on the window during a SwiftUI update is the regression to remove, not to add. Main thread: the replacement stays on main, off the WebKit callback stack. Do not call it via `DispatchQueue.main.sync`. Doctrine: no tenant config. The web view's data store stays the one the tab already had. Localization: any new string uses `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: describe the crash as a lifecycle bug. Do not include a crash-trigger recipe beyond the existing debug hook.

Size: S–M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: a dead web view is replaced later, on the same profile. Terminals keep running.

C11-287 — batch validation handoff preparation

PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/501 (draft)
Head: e4f67eb78eb22eb60944b3a17a8b69d8277865dc
Actor: agent:codex-browser
Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M3X4FNR43RVWK5EDEGFBRQYF.md

The Orchestrator's adopted batch-validation flow supersedes the earlier per-ticket Atlas runtime blocker. Runtime recovery, rendering, inspector teardown, snapshot, and focus measurements remain unperformed by the owner. The Atlas Validator will run the following scenario on merged main. CI and targeted behavioral test results will be recorded separately before HANDOFF REVIEW; a green build does not itself prove these visible paths.

Validator scenario

1. Build merged main as a uniquely tagged Debug app on Atlas. Launch with C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh using launch-tagged-automation.sh. Record merged SHA, tag, binary path, automation socket, display enumeration, and load average. Confine all UI input to the verified display and this tagged window, with a hard stop timer and proven synthesized dismissal. Expected: startup dialogs suppressed and production c11/agents untouched.
2. Create a readable side-by-side terminal and browser area. Load https://example.com (synthetic public fixture). Capture a screenshot, current URL, and an interactive browser snapshot. Type a unique synthetic marker in the terminal and read it back. Expected: both areas paint, terminal responds, and snapshot returns a nonempty DOM tree.
3. Invoke DEBUG socket method debug.browser.simulate_web_content_termination for the browser's workspace_id/tab_id. Wait for the queued turn and page completion. Record browser.webview.replace log entries, URL, screenshot, terminal marker readback, and Ghostty log. Expected: one replacement after scheduling, same URL restored, terminal accepts input, no host/terminal crash. The pre-replacement return and same-turn duplicate coalescing are covered by the targeted host and gate tests; do not infer callback timing solely from a socket round trip.
4. Start a fresh browser tab on the same fixture. Simulate termination, wait for replacement, then simulate again within ten seconds. Expected: the second replacement paints the existing error page and does not automatically reload the URL. Simulate again within that window. Expected: no third makeWebView/replacement log entry, no busy recovery loop. Repeat on an initially empty tab: its first replacement remains the new-tab state, its second reaches the existing error page, and its third does not replace. Record logs/screenshots and elapsed times.
5. On a recovered browser beside the terminal, resize the split in both directions, switch away/back, and capture screenshots after each. Expected: readable areas and painted page after both split resize and crash recovery. No window-wide forced display or immediate SwiftUI layout flush is required. Run one live browser snapshot again. Expected: a nonempty tree; H-E automation fixes are not part of this PR.
6. Open Web Inspector through the tagged app's UI. Capture before/after screenshots while (a) closing its owning browser tab with a terminal surviving, (b) closing its owning browser window with another tagged window/terminal surviving, and (c) simulating a crash while the inspector is open. Expected: inspector closes before old host teardown; no host crash or queued reopen of a closed tab; surviving terminal input works; crash replacement preserves inspector restore intent. Also quit/relaunch the tagged app with an inspector open, proving clean dismissal and no teardown crash.
7. Inspect targeted CI results for WebContentReplacementGateTests, the six termination tests in BrowserSessionHistoryRestoreTests, and BrowserLifecycleRegressionTests. Expected: behavioral assertions pass for stale/closed work, blank/nonblank cap, inspector teardown ordering, duplicate/case-varied synthetic download query resolution (first value wins), and exactly-once popup cancellation with a missing controller plus ordinary allowed navigation. These download/popup cases run through executable seams, not source greps. If host CI omits results or reports an advisory failure, run these classes on the Atlas rail and record the actual result.
8. Compare a short browser/terminal focus-and-input sequence against a tagged origin/main baseline from before this change, using the same fixture, geometry, display, and probe. Record both timings and both load averages; no fleet soak. Expected: surviving terminal focus/input remains responsive and no new typing stall is observed. Capture the result and dismiss the tagged app with synthesized input; verify its window/process is gone.

Local evidence already observed: lane-only commits pushed, clean git diff --check, project-file syntax accepted by plutil, installed c11-browser commands reference synced and byte-equal. No owner runtime claims, no merge/release, and no next ticket started. Validator failures route back to this same ticket for a forward fix.

## Blocking

1. **Raw mode still implicitly submits.** `Sources/SendTextParse.swift:17,45-48`; `CLI/c11.swift:3042`; `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py:207`. `c11 send --tab <target> --raw 'echo example'` leaves `submit = true`, so it schedules a separate Return and executes the line. The same is true of `paste`. The live test expressly expects an extra Return for `send --raw -`, without any explicit submit option. This contradicts this cycle's review brief: raw sends the given bytes with no implicit Return. The stored implementation plan and current documentation instead preserve default submission and require `--no-submit`; this is a concrete contract disagreement, not an undiscovered runtime edge. Smallest fix under the review brief: make raw/paste suppress the extra Return by default, preserve ordinary send's existing default, and update behavioral tests/help/skill accordingly. Explicit `send-key enter` already supplies submission. If the release owner intends the plan's different contract, the review brief needs an explicit correction before this can pass. The ticket's stated C0-control exclusion remains valid; this finding concerns the additional Return.

2. **The new large UTF-8 stdin path crosses a lossy framing seam, with no large-input proof.** `CLI/c11.swift:3040-3051` sends the whole stdin string through JSON to the unchanged `Sources/TerminalController.swift:2030-2039`. That reader decodes each at-most-4095-byte socket read independently, replacing the entire chunk with an empty string if UTF-8 decoding fails. A long stdin document containing multibyte characters can split one character across reads; both fragments fail decoding, discarding whole chunks. The outcome can be invalid JSON or missing document text. `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py:204-208` exercises only tiny ASCII inputs; the retained runtime driver invokes those same cases. Thus the brief's large-text/no-truncation requirement is neither established nor supported by the full path. This is a statically identified inherited seam, not a claimed new regression or an executed reproduction. Smallest fix: coordinate with C11-140's existing framing ownership, preserve bytes until a complete newline-delimited request is assembled, then decode; add an Atlas behavioral case that forces UTF-8 splits and compares the complete large stdin payload at the PTY. No new ticket or wider I/O rewrite is needed.

3. **Queued newline/no-submit acceptance remains unproved.** `tests_v2/test_send_raw_and_flags.py:239-256`. The actual queue scenario sends a literal backslash+n string and a suffix, then checks screen text and absence of `command not found`. It never queues real leading/trailing/newline-only content or stdin, and does not inspect bytes or Return outside the paste envelope after flush. The two host tests inspect the pending queue before attach; they do not exercise the eventual Ghostty/PTY flush. Plan acceptance 3 explicitly requires repeating the newline cases on the queued-before-attach path. The existing proof would miss newline conversion or an extra Return during attach. Smallest fix: extend the bounded queue fixture's Atlas runtime proof to those inputs with an exact byte/Return oracle across flush, retaining full-text events and queued/delivered booleans. This is a missing required proof, not a claim that the new queue helper is demonstrably broken.

data.body:
# C11-314 validation

Actor agent:grok-flaky. Head d1d6cee460baa0c913832709c5af4142bb4ab029. Clean tree, empty overlay.

## What changed

Deleted the cases the c11 1.0 run recorded as flaky:

- WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests.testRemoteRelayMetadataCleanupScriptPreservesDifferentSocketAddr (31.3s, C11-306)
- WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests.testRemoteRelayMetadataCleanupScriptRemovesMatchingSocketAddr (31.512s, C11-263)
- WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests.testRemoteCommandIsRefusedAfterSuccessfulHandshake (16.0s, C11-306)
- WorkspaceRemoteConnectionTests.testProxyOnlyErrorsKeepSSHWorkspaceConnectedAndLoggedInSidebar (nil unwrap on both main class controls)
- MessagesPageTests.testWriterMaxWaitRunsDuringSteadyTraffic (30ms wait, Batch 2)

Kept testRemoteCommandRelayDoesNotStartListener. It already checks the ssh-unavailable start refusal with no wait. Kept testSSHAgentEnvVarsPropagateToSpawnedProcess. It was not recorded as flaky.

No existing non-timing test covers cleanup-script matching versus preserve, post-handshake command refusal, proxy-only sidebar state, or max-wait under steady traffic. Those behaviors are deleted outright. No product code.

Three SocketControlPasswordStoreTests lazy-keychain cases passed a nil file URL, so loadPassword read the build host's socket password file and never called the injected loader. They now use a missing file. The class is not deleted.

No other October comment recorded a test as flaky. ShellGitWatcherTests was a PermissionError fixed forward on C11-305.

## Atlas proof

Expect all 60 UUIDs/layouts restored. Cycle all 60 again; verify selected body/content each time, <=3 mounts during real handoff/priming, and exactly the selected body after settlement. PR #514. Head `e6c893cd119730137808f0d2e2c5836799d83d67`; base `14fd85a5a6e68878fca6e009619d953188eb2471` (merge-base with fetched origin/main). ## Blocking

None found.

The production admission overload bounds pending background mounts to one, independently of queue size. It preserves an existing selected workspace and a genuine retiring workspace, deduplicates those against pending admission, retains the admitted pending load, and promotes the next queued workspace after removal. Debug fixture pins remain an explicit exemption. Reconciliation consumes the emitted pending set rather than the pre-update @Published property. The existing two-second timeout and headless demand paths remain intact.

Unmounting removes presentation trees without deleting Workspace/TerminalTab models or freeing their owned terminal runtime. Sidebar notification, agent-state and flag projection reads those models and stores independently of the mounted content subset. Selection inserts a cold workspace into the mount set; existing presentation rules keep only the selected workspace input-active. The patch does not change TabItemView equality, input/hitTest/forceRefresh paths, telemetry threading, persistence schemas, tenant configuration or user-facing strings. New Swift tests execute the production admission policy; the socket fixture reads runtime events and terminal output rather than source text.

## Non-blocking

1. `tests_v2/test_background_workspace_mount_cap.py:95`: strengthen the per-switch oracle. If socket selection changes for first/middle/last but the presentation never reconciles, the loop checks only workspace.current; the later check can accept the pre-switch settled event for the original workspace. Thus the script can report successful switch settlement without observing those intermediate mounts. Smallest improvement: after each select, wait for a fresh reconcile sample naming that target and containing its mount ID. This is non-blocking because the separately required batch UI scenario explicitly checks each selected body's visible content, including all 60 workspaces.

## Runtime proof still required

The owner's validation comment `ev_01M3XNRDYN71HE0RPYQQ9JT2QS` records patch/syntax checks and a future Validator scenario, not executed behavioral evidence. The plan explicitly batch-defers tagged runtime acceptance for this ticket; that authorized deferral does not block this static verdict. It does not establish product acceptance.

The Atlas batch Validator must execute the documented isolated tagged-app baseline/candidate scenario with debug retention disabled:

- Run the 60-workspace socket fixture: retain all workspace models, observe at most two mounts during background priming and three during a genuine handoff, promote the entire queue through ready/timeout completion, and settle to the selected body alone.
- Read/send to an actually unmounted later queue member, observe executed synthetic output and unchanged selection/focused tab, and preserve existing terminal output/scrollback. Confirm agent status, notifications and flags still reach its sidebar row while its content is unmounted.
- Use the real tagged UI to select/cycle all 60 workspaces during creation and after graceful shutdown/QA resume. Verify restored UUIDs and split layout, readable selected content, no persistent blank panels, no input-active retiring workspace, and mount bounds during switches and settlement.
- Record exact baseline/candidate SHAs, host load, mount logs, creation/settlement/switch timings and screenshots. Enumerate the validation display, enforce the stated timer and prove dismissal. Runtime validation and release sign-off remain outstanding.

# C11-298 review (Grok), cycle 1

Verdict: **PASS** at `876fbadf08aacb56af4f62202259716f9de111e5` (base `7edd59b882df9a6c5eda80566d34514acdd1b332`).

A second copy of the fixed app yields and exits. It does not signal the running instance. Arbitration is a total order. The production socket is still owned by the incumbent, because the newcomer leaves before workspace, sentinel, or socket startup. Sparkle's relaunch path still replaces the app only after the old process has exited. The rollout limit is recorded, not claimed away. No `runModal` was added. The tests call the policy and, in the guest oracle, a real launch.

## Blocking

None.

## What the diff does

`enforceSingleInstance` and `observeDuplicateLaunches` are gone. Both used `terminate()` and, on the immediate `isTerminated` check, `forceTerminate()`. The replacement is `SingleInstancePolicy` (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:14`) plus `AppDelegate.yieldToRunningInstanceIfNeeded()` (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:13320`), called from `cmuxApp.init` after the launch-manifest and untagged-debug checks and before `WorkspaceManager`, Ghostty setup, and `appDelegate.configure` (`Sources/c11App.swift:205`). `configure` is what starts the socket (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:3443`).

A candidate is a live, same-bundle-id process whose own executable matches the main executable declared by that process's bundle, after symlink resolution (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:25`). The embedded CLI paths are excluded even when the metadata matches (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:42`). Helpers whose executable is not that bundle's declared main executable are not candidates. Different bundle ids (tagged vs production, or two tags) do not compete (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:65`).

The winner is finished-over-unfinished, then missing launch date treated as oldest, then earlier date, then lower PID (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:72`). Both sides of each pair are tested, so two contenders that see the same snapshot cannot both yield. The loser activates the winner and `Darwin._exit(0)` (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:13351`). There is no terminate, no save, and no modal.

`UpdateController` is lazy (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:2348`). Its initializer applies Sparkle defaults, including writing the migration flag (`Sources/Update/UpdateController.swift:76` and `Sources/Update/UpdateController.swift:23`). A newcomer that exits never constructs it. `applicationDidFinishLaunching` now only schedules Launch Services registration (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:2872`).

`scheduleSelfRelaunchAfterExit` is unchanged: a detached helper waits until `kill -0` fails, then `open -n` (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:3419`). That is the app-restart path. The signed update samples show the same shape for Sparkle: old PID 623 disappears, the sample set is empty, then PID 3966 appears about 211ms later, with no overlapping sample and no `instance.yield` in that trace. Premature build 29802 (PID 1829) yielded to running 29801 and left the shell, heartbeat child, graph, socket, and supplied persistence in place (`art_01M3Y551F6ZKGVT96FNW1DK7KB`). The quit screenshot is the existing "Quit c11?" sheet. This diff does not touch quit confirmation.

The older-binary limit is stated in the plan and in the oracle: both sides must already contain the fix, because a running older binary still has the killer observer (`tests_v2/test_single_instance_yield.py:23`). The new policy never signals another process (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:12`). That limit is not hidden.

## Inconclusive same-path repeat

Not a blocking gap. At this head, a same-path `open -n -W` did not return, and the run was reported inconclusive rather than PASS. The newcomer had already logged `instance.yield` and exited, which is the fleet-preserving outcome. The yield function is the one that passed the full same-path and copied-path oracle at parent `c7351e3ff4` (`art_01M3XWPN8APH5YV3X2MP2A7SFV`), including `open -W` returning. Exact-head proof covers the harder identity case (a second bundle path, same id) and the signed Sparkle replacement. The python oracle's wait (`tests_v2/test_single_instance_yield.py:229` and `:259`) is the piece that did not finish on the same-path repeat. That is an honest residual on the waiter, not an unproven kill of the running fleet.

## Tests and doctrine

`SingleInstancePolicyTests` (ten cases in `c11Tests/SocketControlSafetyTests.swift:355`) call the policy: scan order, PID tie-break, terminated and other-bundle-id processes, missing metadata, CLI and helper executables, finished-vs-unfinished, missing dates, and copied plus symlinked bundles on disk. They do not grep source. The guest script launches `open -n` and checks PIDs, socket inode, graph ids, heartbeat, and the unsaved shell marker. No new user-facing string. No `runModal` on this path. No tenant-config write. Not a typing or socket-command path; the one `activate` is the explicit duplicate app launch, which is the specified user-visible result. XCTest and `CMUX_UI_TEST_*` still skip arbitration (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:2218` and `:13323`), so a packaged launch is not exempt.

The numbered validator scenario in the handoff comment matches the acceptance: same bundle, copied bundle, helper left alive, second tag, warn-on Cancel and Quit, warn-off Quit, restart after the old PID exits, and signed premature-yield plus real update. Those runs were executed for this head, except the same-path waiter noted above and the helper observation retained from the parent head. The scenario is adequate.

## Non-blocking

1. `c11UITests/MultiWindowNotificationsUITests.swift:234` still sets `CMUX_UI_TEST_ENABLE_DUPLICATE_LAUNCH_OBSERVER`. Nothing reads it. The test does not assert duplicate-launch behavior, so this is not a false green. Delete the assignment.

2. Two cold starts that both snapshot `runningApplications` before either is visible can both see no incumbent and both continue (`Sources/AppDelegate.swift:13347`). The plan's self-only recheck was not kept. A live socket is not unlinked (`Sources/TerminalController.swift:1236`); the second process binds an alternate (`Sources/TerminalController.swift:1334`). The production socket still has one owner, and a second fleet can remain until one quits. data.from:
## Why
The operator needs to collapse a fleet into folders without hiding the worker that needs attention, and move workspaces between folders directly in the sidebar. Backlog item: W2.

## Evidence
- c11: `Sources/ContentView.swift:8392-8408,8535-8536` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) is the SwiftUI WorkspaceSidebar and workspace list. `Sources/ContentView.swift:8572-8576,8598-8638` precomputes activity/unread and carries flagged/suppressed attention into row values.
- Upstream: cmux #4815/#5018 introduced groups. At upstream/main (920ff39ff7), `Sources/SidebarWorkspaceGroupHeaderView.swift` is an Equatable header but doubles as an anchor workspace; `Sources/SidebarWorkspaceGroupContextMenuRunner.swift` and `Sources/SidebarWorkspaceReorderDropView.swift` are interaction references. Follow-up bugs #5253, #8925, #9176, #13688 and #15892 warn against copying the anchor model.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` proposal §3; Fable audit row 4.12; Astra audit rows 4.12/4.12b. BACKLOG.md D17/W2 makes folders core despite the older deferral in `c11-1.0.html` §4; automatic root filing stays cut.

## Scope
In: W1 folder headers with chevron, icon, name, member count and attention badge; collapse/expand, drag to join/leave/reorder, group context menu, six translations and accessibility labels.
Out: anchor-workspace semantics, generated anchor terminals, automatic root filing, automatic naming, AppKit sidebar rewrite, redesigning the attention state machine or Feed (A1-A4), W4 history, Recently Closed and stable tab numbers. W1 owns persistence and CLI; W3 owns integrated scale/sign-off evidence.

## Approach
Project W1's folder records and current per-tab attention into immutable header values. Keep expensive aggregation outside typing-hot row bodies, preserving existing Equatable optimization. Reserve badge/label space so changing counts and hover controls do not shift hit targets. Violet represents any flagged member, including flagged-and-suppressed; the waiting count excludes suppressed tabs, while unread follows the existing notification definition. A collapsed header must retain the flag signal. Specify drop targets and pinned-segment behavior using W1's move core, including empty and collapsed folders. Context menu exposes Rename, Color, Icon, Pin/Unpin, Ungroup and Delete; deletion follows W1's non-destructive membership contract. Use the existing confirmation pattern if any explicitly destructive member-close action is later proposed; it is not required here.

## Acceptance criteria
1. In the real tagged sidebar, create populated and empty folders via W1; every header shows its chevron, icon, name and correct member count. Collapse hides only member rows, and expand restores the same order without starting or closing any terminal.
2. A fixture containing one unsuppressed waiting tab, one suppressed waiting tab, unread notifications and a flagged-and-suppressed tab shows waiting count one and a violet flag. Collapse, then raise/lower flags on hidden members: the visible header updates correctly without requiring expansion. Unread agrees with member notification records; removing the final flag restores the ordinary badge state.
3. Pointer-driven drags cover ungrouped to folder, folder to ungrouped, folder to folder, within-folder reorder, empty/collapsed targets and cancelled/outside drops. Each changes exactly the intended membership/order, obeys W1 pin semantics, and preserves unrelated workspaces and tab identities.
4. Every context-menu action changes the intended folder only. Ungroup/Delete preserves the members and running work; closing the first member never promotes another into a special anchor role.
5. With an unrelated terminal accepting typed input, badge changes do not move controls, hide the active terminal or steal keyboard/app focus. Group updates issued through non-focus CLI commands have the same preservation behavior.
6. New visible and accessibility strings render in English and all six locales; JSON is valid and interpolation tokens are preserved. Long labels and changing counts remain usable at narrow sidebar widths, in Light/Dark theme slots and with keyboard/VoiceOver navigation.

## Validation
Add behavioral attention-projection and drop-planner tests, including the suppressed-flag fixture. Use tests_v2 against a tagged socket for setup/oracles, then fresh-context computer use to drive actual drag/drop, menus, collapse and focus; retain screenshots. W3 repeats at 50+ workspaces and supplies Atin's numbered sign-off script. Compare typing under attention/drop churn against F2 budgets; builds and soaks run on Atlas once F1/C11-216 lands, using the build lock and tagged QA launch. No passing claim based only on socket mutations or source-string tests.

## Dependencies
W1 is required. F1 (C11-216) supplies Atlas builds; F2 supplies baseline/budgets. A1/A3 are adjacent attention changes to coordinate with, not a requirement to rebuild their logic here. W3 consumes the integrated sidebar. The lead links cross-workstream dependencies.

## Risks
Sidebar observation breadth and per-member aggregation can regress typing/main-thread responsiveness. Do not add work to hitTest outside pointer handling or forceRefresh. Pin/drop ambiguity and collapse can hide attention unless the explicit fixture passes. No tenant config writes. Six-locale localization and accessible fixed geometry are part of delivery. Sanitize public screenshots, names and paths.

Size: L. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: a visible folder primitive and projection of existing attention; no task inference, auto-answering or agent configuration writes.

The owner must publish the frozen protocol, script hashes, source/build identity and reviewed calibration specification before collecting one matched pair. Every attempt gets a new immutable directory. Do not reset a failed attempt, adjust thresholds, extend phases, pool phases, or retry a failed metric.

## Artifacts and conditions

Both are built before reservation via the authorized remote-build route. ## Quiet window and UI safety

Coordinate non-build work through the Orchestrator. `quiet_window.py hold` uses a separate guardian that alone owns the real slot-1 then slot-2 flock descriptors. It never deletes lock files. Slow process snapshots are taken by its supervisor and cannot delay the guardian. First successful flock starts a 2700-second cap; waiting for slot 2/quiet consumes it. Guardian checks every 100 ms, begins closing before the deadline, closes FDs before writing release evidence, and also closes on supervisor EOF, interrupt, error, atomic release request or contamination. The pre-first-lock wait is bounded too.

Guardian records load at 1 Hz continuously across both roles and the interval. Supervisor captures host process CPU/RSS every 10 seconds with a bounded subprocess. No role starts unless 1-minute load <8. Once quiet readiness is declared, any load >=8 stops/revokes the attempt and retains the raw sample. Classify from process/host evidence: unrelated work or uncertain attribution is INCOMPLETE; product-attributable sustained load is a regression to diagnose. No automated resampling. Budget failures also remain failures.

`ui_slot.py take` now reserves the shared UI lock before launch. It verifies the assigned stopped app's exact sealed bundle/executable hashes and rejects an existing tagged process/socket. It creates a permanent once-role claim, then starts a detached supervisor. The supervisor forks the exact bundle executable behind a **closed launch pipe**, records its PID, and publishes readiness before the parent can send launch permission. The supervisor owns/reaps that child for its entire lifetime, so PID reuse cannot redirect cleanup; no kqueue/ps/bootstrap AppKit call sits in the deadline path. The 1200-second cap starts at reservation, including bootstrap and launch. Both roles exec with identical QA-fresh/automation/tagged-socket/log environment isolation, recorded in the lease. This replaces unbounded prelaunch via LaunchServices.

Initial state reads, fork, readiness writes and all later checks are inside supervised cleanup. Before launch permission, parent failure closes the gate without executing an app. Between launch and acknowledged handoff, parent EOF/exception requests cleanup. Later, the independent supervisor enforces its cap and pair revocation. Cleanup kills only its unreaped owned child; no PID rediscovery. File/write/Popen/readiness errors roll back only inode-and-token-owned reservations after cleanup is proven. Preserve partial role evidence by archiving it; the permanent role claim forbids a retry in the same attempt. A foreign lock is never deleted. If exact-child cleanup is unproven, leave the reservation occupied and fail closed. A forced dismissal is failed evidence, never synthesized-dismissal proof.

Normal release requires saved, reviewed synthesized Command-Q/dialog evidence for the exact child PID and the supervisor's successful reap. Release removes only the owned UI lock. Candidate reservation requires control's successful normal dismissal. No `open`, old shell-wrapper launch, prelaunched PID adoption, or app launch outside this reservation belongs in the measurement runbook.

The four appearance settings are **observations**, not spec values. Before template capture, require an externally reviewed record of actual theme, font, scale and sidebar width, tied to the immutable `setup-config.json` SHA, `setup.png` SHA, exact PID/window/display/artifact identity and observation evidence references. Calibrate compares observations to the sealed specification before populating measurement config. Run admission and comparison revalidate that same evidence. Intended baseline geometry (200-point sidebar, display 9 at 1920x1080, window 1320x880) alone is insufficient.

## Primary measurements and deterministic mutations

Three fixed 60-second phases: no-churn, churn, quiescence. Each schedules 105 typing, 42 switch, 42 real HID sidebar scroll probes in the first 58 seconds: repeat [typing x5, switch x2, scroll x2] 21 times at index*58/189. Trial timeout is one second, with capture-end minus posted-input time and no overhead subtraction. Retain every failed/precondition/timeout/setup-exception row, setup/capture overhead, all monotonic timestamps, templates and crop evidence. No implicit stop/recalibration after three failed probes. Minimum valid counts per metric per phase: 100/40/40.

Churn schedules exactly 600 mutation RPCs at start+n/10 (n=0...599), one in flight, and joins by the 60-second boundary. Repeat categories reorder, transfer, flag, waiting_suppression. Exactly 150 per category. Reorders alternate w25/w26 across w60 using absolute final indices. Transfers alternate w27/w28 between Move Lane and ungrouped, appending in the matching pin segment. Flags alternate w10/w46 and toggle flag state: 75 raises, 75 lowers. Waiting updates alternate w11/w45 and toggle suppression over the fixed exact unread notifications: 76 suppressions and 74 unsuppressions. This exercises collapsed and offscreen members while keeping w01/w02 and the first 24 unpinned workspace identities in place.

Per-operation records include intended time, start/end, method/category/params, response/errors, independent expected canonical order/membership/attention, and selected workspace before/after. The worker's non-focus selection observations and the real UI switch trial are serialized by one in-process lock, so an explicit switch cannot masquerade as focus theft. Both roles use this same synchronization and the same additional read queries; they are part of the declared workload. Each successful visible switch also queries and records its actual selected ID. Read RPC overhead is retained and may make a rate shortfall visible; never silently reduce checks or extend the phase.

At phase boundaries verify exact complete unique workspace/tab identities, pin bits, membership, canonical order, attention, notification state, shell identities, selection, group metadata/order and derived member counts. Retain raw trees and resource snapshots (CPU/RSS/VSZ/footprint, including footprint/IOSurface output). The worker must be joined with no pending work before quiescence. Capture existing tagged hang telemetry and any available header recomputation observations separately; do not invent missing instruments.

## Acceptance and separate functional evidence

Nearest-rank percentiles from valid raw samples, per metric/per phase. All 18 must pass: candidate p95 <= max(control*1.20, control+5ms), candidate p99 <= max(control*1.25, control+15ms). At 42 samples p99 is the maximum. Keep prior failed trials even when valid minima pass. Malformed/missing evidence or count/rate/phase overrun is INCOMPLETE. Late starts are reported, not a new per-operation budget.

`compare.py` checks raw samples/PNGs/templates, phase schedule, frozen mutation replay and matched semantic fixture, attention/identity assertions, required source/artifact/harness provenance, observed prime logs, matched warmup, continuous quiet load and normal bounded UI dismissal. All 60 workspace/tab identities, pins, 56 shell PID/start identities, group properties/projections, attention and notifications remain checked; only declared collapse/expand, reorder and membership changes are allowed. This helper does not prove the remaining menu/focus/mount or ticket UI scenarios.

Coalesced per main turn and cheap per call, but it is the one O(all members) refresh in the churn phase. If C11-261 shows it, the smallest fix is a per-workspace dirty set keyed off the notification's `workspaceId` instead of a global flag.
   - `Sources/ContentView.swift:8821` (`groupHeader`) — `WorkspaceColorSettings.palette()` reads UserDefaults (`defaultOverrideMap` + `customColorEntries`) once per header per sidebar body evaluation. Hoist to one `let palette = WorkspaceColorSettings.palette()` at the top of `body` next to `chromeTokens`.
   - `Sources/ContentView.swift:8547` — `workspacesById` dictionary is rebuilt on every sidebar body evaluation (O(N)). Fine at 60; noted for completeness.
2. **Unread definition deviates from the plan text and is disclosed only in the PR body.** Plan item 4 says the header sums `notificationStore.unreadCount(forWorkspaceId:)`; the code uses the new `rawUnreadCount(forWorkspaceId:)` (`TerminalNotificationStore.swift:951`), which includes suppressed entries. Observable effect: a suppressed worker with three unread notifications shows no unread on its own row (rows still use `unreadCount`) while its folder header shows unread 3; expanding the folder shows no row carrying it. The skill text ("counts workspace notification records exactly once") matches the code, and the ticket's own Approach line ("unread follows the existing notification definition") is ambiguous. Not a correctness bug, but the Orchestrator should record the ruling on the ticket so C11-261's sign-off script and C11-291's strings describe the same number.
3. **Dead code left behind.** `SidebarDropPlanner.indicator(...)` (`Sources/ContentView.swift:14598`) and `SidebarDropPlanner.targetIndex(...)` (`:14638`) no longer have callers (only `edgeForPointer` is used); `c11Tests/SidebarOrderingTests.swift` now tests unreachable code. 4. **Dropping a member on its own folder header moves it to the end of that folder.** `WorkspaceGroupDropPlanner.plan` `.groupBody` → `transfer` appends after the last same-pin member even when the source is already in the group. The preview shows the move, so it is not surprising mid-drag, but a slip onto the header reorders the folder. Smallest fix: in `.groupBody`, when `original.groupId == groupId`, return an unchanged plan (`changed: false`).
5. **Shift-click anchor changed from last-clicked row to the selected workspace** (`ContentView.swift:13597`). When the selected workspace is inside a collapsed folder, `selectionRange` returns nil and Shift-click degrades to a plain click. 6. **`dropExited` clears the indicator unconditionally** (`ContentView.swift:15071`). With nested targets (header body vs. the groupControls lane vs. the empty area) the exit of the old target can fire after the new target's `dropEntered`, blanking the preview for one update. 8. **Planner refuses every drop in a window that holds an orphan `groupId`** (`WorkspaceGroupDropPlanner.swift:62` throws `invalidSnapshot`) while the projection intentionally renders the orphan as an ungrouped row. Only reachable through a corrupted session file; if W1 ever lets one through, drag silently stops working window-wide. C11-231.title: Expose journal-backed agent snapshots, waiting reasons, clocks and restore candidates

data.from: waiting.entered and waiting.exited carry surface and reason
data.to: Expose journal-backed agent snapshots, waiting reasons, clocks and restore candidates

data.from: Why: verified 2026-09-23 on the live events file: waiting.entered carries only instance, seq, ts, type, v, workspace. No surface, no reason. Probe 1 counted 154 waiting events in one run workspace and 492 in another on 2026-07-31 and could not say which surface waited or why, so starvation and attention-flooding are unmeasurable. Deliverable: waiting.entered and waiting.exited carry surface (UUID) and a reason enum (agent_prompt, permission, flag, unknown) in payload; docs updated and synced; a test through the real event path. Out of scope: changing the sidebar attention model.
data.to:
## Why
Overwatch and the operator need to distinguish a blocked ask from an unread completion and see why each tab waits, without scraping multiple inconsistent surfaces. Backlog item: J6.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- Existing C11-231 records 154 and 492 workspace waiting events in two observed runs with no way to identify the waiting tab or reason; expand that ticket, do not create a duplicate.
- c11: `Sources/Events/EventEmitter.swift:138` accepts optional surface but emits no reason; `Sources/Events/EventEnvelope.swift:51`–`:52` name waiting.entered/waiting.left (the old ticket calls the latter exited). `Sources/TabLivenessDeriver.swift:13` conflates notification and waiting. `Sources/TabSheetDetail.swift:32` and `:49` source state/turn clocks separately; `Sources/TabSeenClock.swift:151` supplies seen time.
- Upstream: #14870 crash session listing; `Packages/macOS/CmuxAgentJournal/Sources/CmuxAgentJournal/AgentJournalReplayPolicy.swift:24`. Research: BACKLOG.md J6; report 01 Waiting changes meaning/What the journal unlocks; Fable §7 roster; Astra §7 honest state contract.

## Scope
In: c11 agents --json; lifecycle.changed; attributable waiting reason events; blocked versus unread-completion projection; journal-backed tab-sheet clocks; historical crash-live session list for restore. Out: redesigning sidebar/⌥V ordering, Feed UI/replies, auto-resuming sessions, restore recipe/account changes, focus-history persistence and changing suppression policy.

## Approach
Project a single read snapshot from J2 plus existing identity, flag/suppressed and seen stores. Include kind, model, state, reason, since, source, freshness, flag, suppressed and last_seen_at per tab. Emit lifecycle.changed {tab, agent, from, to, reason} only on actual transitions; keep the existing events stream best-effort and make snapshot refresh the recovery route. Satisfy C11-231 with attributable waiting.entered/waiting.left reason payloads or an explicitly reviewed compatibility mapping, never silently rename left to exited. Project old blocked/error as unconfirmed and keep raw blocking separate from attention presentation.

## Acceptance criteria
1. For F3’s two-tab case, agents --json identifies tab A’s blocked reason and source while tab B works; includes every required field and explicit null/unavailable values where observation is missing.
2. Opening a blocked tab updates seen information without claiming its ask answered. Opening an unread completion clears only unread attention; flags and suppression preserve their existing routing behavior.
3. The C11-231 incident can be analyzed from events: a real transition carries the exact tab/agent and reason, repeated identical observations do not create duplicate lifecycle edges, and waiting event compatibility is documented.
4. Tab-sheet state/turn clocks match the recorded F3 timestamps and remain stable through a restart; history restored as unconfirmed does not claim current liveness or invent elapsed work through a coverage gap.
5. The restore-candidate list identifies sessions with start but no end at crash, labels them historical candidates, and distinguishes ended/unknown sessions without launching anything.
6. For disconnected/degraded sources and a deliberately dropped telemetry interval, a fresh agents snapshot gives the known state, provenance and freshness without moving focus.

## Validation
Use projection/clock fixtures from F3 and behavioral event-stream tests, then tests_v2 against an isolated tagged socket for agents and lifecycle.changed. Independently drive seen/blocked/completion/suppression and tab-sheet UI with computer use (verified display, timer, dismissal). Run native builds and the F2 snapshot/event-load soak on Atlas after C11-216.

## Dependencies
Depends on J2. This is the expanded C11-231 scope and closes its waiting-reason requirement when implemented. Coordinate A2 Feed and workspace restore work (existing C11-131/C11-139) through the lead; no automatic resume is added. J8 owns matching skill updates and installed sync.

## Risks
Keep disk/parsing/aggregation off main and out of typing hot paths. Bound retained data and diagnostics. Localize new UI strings in ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; preserve format tokens. Sanitize public fixtures/logs; never retain prompt or tool bodies. Apply docs/aar-c11-188-attention-loop.md: evaluate the named fixtures/questions, cap review/fix cycles at three, and escalate non-convergence instead of expanding the contract.

Size: M. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: optional observation and c11-owned storage only; no tenant configuration writes, automatic answers or trust broadening.
